title: Lineup-apply loop resolved --matchup dates to the weekly Scoring Period number, not the daily period, causing duplicate Pushover storms
description:
internal/lineuprun.go's per-date apply loop (used by both optimize and shadow via internal/lineuprun.Run) resolved each --dates/--matchup date to a Fantrax scoring period via fantrax.ResolvePeriod(periods, currentPeriod, seasonStart, today, date), introduced by rosterbot-z3b (2026-07-12). ResolvePeriod's tier 1 trusts periods (from GetScoringPeriodsAndTeams) as an authoritative per-DAY period map, but that list is actually the weekly matchup 'Scoring Period' schedule (~7 days/period, wider around breaks). Since virtually every in-season date falls inside some weekly period's date range, tier 1 won on nearly every call, overriding the correct daily anchor arithmetic (tiers 2/3).

Discovered 2026-07-14 investigating user report of repeated duplicate Pushover lineup-change notifications. The All-Star break merged two weeks into weekly period 16 (2026-07-13..07-26). Every hourly Lineup Fargate run (12x/day, optimize --matchup) evaluated --matchup dates 2026-07-16 through 2026-07-26 (11 distinct calendar dates), and ALL of them resolved to period 16 via ResolvePeriod tier 1. Confirmed via CloudWatch logs (log group InfraStack-Logs6819BB44-evRuHY7lXtHK): GetHitterRosterForPeriod(16)/GetPitcherRosterForPeriod(16) fetched the identical stale snapshot for all 11 dates, ApplyLineup(16, ...) wrote all 11 dates' changes to the same period, and because each date's real target-day diff never converged, the identical lineup swap (same players, same +25.93 pts, same 'locked players -- retrying without 9 player(s)' apply-rejection) re-applied and re-fired a Pushover notification for all 11 dates on every single hourly run -- 11 duplicate notifications/hour, hour after hour.

This is the same architectural flaw as rosterbot-uv6 (GetTeamGS's daily walk mistakenly routed through the same periods-list-first resolver), which was fixed for that one call site via gsPeriodWalk/dailyPeriodFor bypassing ResolvePeriod entirely. rosterbot-z3b's consolidation reintroduced the identical mistake one call site later (the apply loop) without recognizing the periods list was weekly, not daily -- its own scoping notes assumed GS-budget/gscheck 'agree with ResolvePeriod's tier 1 by construction' without checking whether the apply loop's needs matched tier 1's actual data shape.
design: Fixed by: (1) exporting fantrax.dailyPeriodFor as fantrax.DailyPeriodFor (gs_period_walk.go) as the single source for date-to-daily-period resolution; (2) switching internal/lineuprun.go's apply loop to call DailyPeriodFor directly instead of ResolvePeriod; (3) deleting fantrax.ResolvePeriod and its test file entirely (period_resolver.go/period_resolver_test.go) -- with the apply loop fixed, it had zero remaining production callers, and no safe production use case exists for it: every real caller needs the daily axis, which the weekly periods list structurally cannot provide. FindCurrentPeriod (still used directly by the GS-limit lookup, which correctly wants the weekly number) and DailyPeriodFor now cleanly own their respective axes with no shared resolver conflating them. CLAUDE.md's Fantrax section rewritten to document the two-axis distinction explicitly so a future consolidation doesn't repeat this.
acceptance_criteria: go build/vet/test clean across the repo. TestGSPeriodWalk_MergedAllStarBreakDailyNumbering and TestFindCurrentPeriod_MergedAllStarBreakPeriod (existing regression coverage for the two axes) still pass. Manually verified DailyPeriodFor resolves 2026-07-16..07-26 (today=2026-07-14) to 11 distinct daily periods (114..124), not a collapsed 16. Next deployed hourly Lineup run should show each --matchup date fetching/applying against its own distinct period and converging to 'No changes needed' on subsequent runs instead of re-notifying every hour.
notes: Relates to rosterbot-uv6/rosterbot-wd5 (same bug class, different call site) and rosterbot-uw6 (deferred validation of daily-period numbering across this same ASB merge window, for the GS-tally axis -- still relevant, unaffected by this fix). Not yet deployed as of filing -- fix is committed locally; deploy via push to main (CodeBuild) picks it up on the next scheduled Lineup task launch.
close_reason: fantrax.DailyPeriodFor wired into internal/lineuprun.go's apply loop; fantrax.ResolvePeriod deleted (zero remaining safe callers). Build/vet/test clean; verified 11 distinct daily periods for the merged-ASB date range that previously collapsed to one. Committed, pending push/deploy.

title: Dashboard headline metric (MAE) is near-blind to the model's actual skill
description: Measured over the 850 production grade rows (LEGACY + depthcharts-ros): hitter projections achieve MAE 4.380 vs 4.356 for a constant projection at the sample mean — i.e. -0.5% skill, and -6.0% against the MAE-minimising median baseline (4.132). Cause is that hitter projections barely vary (sd(proj)=0.66) against enormous daily outcome variance (sd(actual)=5.52). MAE at the player-day level is therefore ~all irreducible single-game noise, and the dashboard reports it to three decimals as the scoreboard. The model DOES have real skill, but only rank skill, which is exactly what a lineup optimiser needs: within-day Spearman rho = +0.1218 for hitters (se 0.0373, t=+3.26, positive on 30/40 days) and +0.4292 for pitchers (se 0.0982, t=+4.37, positive on 18/23 days). Both independently reproduced.
design: internal/report aggregates per (window,role); within-day rank correlation needs grouping by dt before correlating, which the current Aggregate does not do. The hindsight gap is the only metric denominated in points the league actually awards.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard leads with decision-relevant metrics: mean within-day Spearman by role, and the realized-vs-hindsight-optimal lineup gap that internal/backtest already computes. MAE remains available as a calibration diagnostic, not the headline.

title: recap-site runtime growing superlinearly — 30d TTL expires immutable past-period snapshots
description: recap-site wall time has grown 192s -> 266s -> 469s -> 483s -> 849s -> 1411s (2026-07-27), with per-week cost tripling from ~33s/wk to ~108s/wk. Mechanism verified from S3 cache object LastModified: 820 'cache/fantrax-pitcher-gs-*' and 817 'cache/fantrax-roster-stats-*' objects were rewritten on Monday 2026-07-20 alone, and the rewrite dates cluster exclusively on Mondays (2026-06-29, 07-06, 07-13, 07-20, 07-27) which is the recap-site schedule. Root cause: pastPeriodTTL = 30*24h at internal/fantrax/cached.go:23 applies to per-period snapshots that CLAUDE.md itself documents as immutable once the period closes. Every Monday rebuild therefore re-fetches every week older than 30 days from Fantrax, including the 200ms/day throttle at internal/fantrax/pitcher_starts.go:107. Cost is O(season length) and compounds weekly; the season runs to ~week 23.
design: Past-period snapshots are immutable by definition, so the natural fix is an effectively-infinite TTL for tierPast rather than 30d. Guard: DailyPeriodFor must be correct about which periods are actually past, otherwise an infinite TTL freezes a live period. Alternative: keep the TTL but make recap-site skip already-rendered weeks (dist/week-NN.html) unless forced.
acceptance_criteria: recap-site wall time stops growing with season length. Past-period snapshot cache entries are not re-fetched once written.

title: No alerting on scheduled task failure — 11-hour outage passed silently
description: The 2026-07-01T17:00Z to 2026-07-02T03:00Z incident ran 11 consecutive failed hourly 'optimize --matchup' runs plus the 23:41Z shadow (all exit=1, STALE_CLIENT) with no notification of any kind. Verified: 'aws cloudwatch describe-alarms' returns zero alarms and 'aws sns list-topics' returns zero topics in us-west-1. The buildnotify Lambda only fires on CodeBuild state-change events, so it covers image builds and not ECS task failures. optimize is the lineup-apply hot path — a silent multi-hour outage there means lineups silently stop being applied on game days.
design: Options: (a) EventBridge rule on ECS Task State Change with stoppedReason/exit code filter -> existing buildnotify-style Lambda -> Pushover; (b) CloudWatch alarm on a run-ledger-derived custom metric. (a) reuses the existing notify path and needs no new metric plumbing. Consider alerting on consecutive-failure count rather than each failure to avoid noise from a single transient.
acceptance_criteria: A repeated-failure signal reaches the operator's Pushover channel within ~2 consecutive failures of any scheduled task. Covers ECS task non-zero exit, not just CodeBuild.

title: League-wide projection grading: grade all 10 rosters, blended vs base, sliced by role/position
description:
## Problem

Projection-system grading is scoped to one team. `cmd/grade.go` calls `ft.DailyFantasyPoints(cfg.TeamID, ...)`, so each system is graded on ~35 player-days/day. Two consequences:

1. **Per-dimension slices are unusable.** `report.PositionRow` buckets C/INF/OF/UT/SP/RP, but our roster carries ~2 catchers — ~60 catcher-days a month. No claim about catcher (or any bucket) projection accuracy is supportable today. The per-role and per-bucket comparison is the actual goal of this work.
2. **We grade the blend, not the system.** `internal/lineuprun/snapshot.go:54` writes `sp.ExpectedPts` — the post-`BlendSources` value (FanGraphs base + trailing-30d/YTD Fantrax production). All four systems converge toward each other as the shared recent-production term takes weight (up to ~28% for hitters). We cannot currently measure whether blending helps or hurts.

Note the headline ranking is NOT the binding constraint: all four systems project the same player-days, so the comparison is paired and day-to-day FPts noise already cancels. Sample size buys the slices, not the top-line number.

## Goal

Grade every projection system against every rostered player in the league, on both the blended and the raw-base value, sliced by hitter/pitcher and by position bucket (C/INF/OF/UT/SP/RP), with a paired significance readout so slice differences are actionable. Enables (a) per-dimension system evaluation and (b) evidence-driven improvement of the blending model.
design:
## Decisions (settled in design interview)

**1. Grade both values per row.** `Projected` stays the blended value (unchanged meaning). Add `ProjectedBase` = raw system per-game projection. `MAE(blend) - MAE(base)` per slice is a first-class output — it is the only way to tell whether blending adds or destroys accuracy, and it directly serves 'improve the blending'.

**2. Population = the 10 fantasy rosters. Free agents are an explicit non-goal.** Rostered-player actuals are already-cached Fantrax bytes; FA actuals would require computing FPts from ~700 MLB statsapi game logs/day via the `mlb_backfill.go` path, which is built for a handful of fetches per window. Selection bias toward rostered players is consistent across all four systems so it does not corrupt the ranking — it only scopes the claim to 'accuracy on rostered players'. Accepted gap: waiver decisions concern unrostered players and get no grading signal (file separately).

**3. Reconstruct at grade time from `.archive/` — do NOT capture forward.** Decisive reason: reconstruction makes grading history **re-runnable**. A capture-based approach freezes every row at that night's blend formula, so a changed window or stabilization constant could only be evaluated going forward. Reconstruction is a pure function of archived bytes, so history re-grades in minutes under a changed hypothesis — the same property that let `backtest --recency-experiment` settle w30-vs-YTD (rosterbot-2nd), extended league-wide. Secondary: backfills to the archive start (~2026-07-02) instead of accumulating from ship date; adds no schedule, no task, nothing to the 23:40 shadow hot path.

Reconstruction needs no schedule/probables replay: `ExpectedPts` is a clean per-game value — `NonStarterSPDiscount` and `hasGame` gating are applied downstream in slot assignment (`internal/optimizer/pitcher_lineup.go:240`), not baked in.

The archive blob for date D is captured at `cron(15 14 * * ? *)` = 10:15am ET, **before any of D's games** — a strictly better grading capture point than shadow's 7:40pm ET.

**4. Extract the blend to a shared pure function.** `(base projection, recent-production series) -> blended per-game`, called by both `internal/lineuprun/blend.go` and the reconstructor. This eliminates the dual-implementation drift risk that plan 3 would otherwise introduce. `hitterWindowBounds` and `collapseHitterWindow` are already pure and client-free, so the extraction is cheap.

**5. Schema is additive columns, no new partitions.** On `analysis.GradeRow`: `ProjectedBase`, `DiffBase`, `FantasyTeamID`, `FantasyTeamName` (denormalized like `teamvalue.Row` so the read path needs no Fantrax call). Repurpose `Source` from snapshot/reconstructed (which goes constant under plan 3) to input provenance: `archive` vs `live-snapshot`. Partition path stays `grades/dt=X/system=Y/` — a third partition dimension means CDK + partition-projection enum churn for a 10-cardinality filter. Old rows carry zero `ProjectedBase` and remain readable. Purely additive: never rewrite existing partitions.

Volume is a non-issue and must not drive the design toward aggregation-on-write: 10 teams x ~40 rostered x 4 systems ~= 1,600 rows/day at ~200B ~= 320KB/day, ~58MB/season in 720 objects. Keep rows atomic.

**6. Scope becomes an explicit dimension in `report.Model`.** Re-key the maps from `window|role` to `scope|window|role`. Without this, league-wide rows silently change the detail views' population and **every trend line gets a step discontinuity on ship day** — pre-ship points are MAE on ~35 selected-for-good players, post-ship are MAE on ~400 including the league tail, drawn as one series. Per-view defaults: system comparison -> league; position table + calibration -> league (this is where N was too thin); misses list -> myteam (a league-wide misses list is 'who had a weird MLB day', not model quality); headline scorecard -> both side by side (the myteam-vs-league MAE gap quantifies how much easier our roster is to project). SPA gets a My Team / League toggle. The `myteam` scope preserves the existing series unbroken.

Scopes have different start dates — myteam-blended runs back to grading start; league-raw backfills only to ~2026-07-02; league-blended only as far back as per-team period snapshots remain fetchable. Charts must render a series beginning mid-axis without implying a drop to zero.

**7. Roster membership comes from `DailyFantasyPoints` per team, NOT `GetFullPlayerPool`.** The pool returns *today's* rosters; using it would retroactively attribute a waiver pickup to their current team for weeks they were not there. `DailyFantasyPoints(teamID, ...)` is derived from per-period roster snapshots and is point-in-time honest, and returns the actuals in the same pass. Team list from `GetScoringPeriodsAndTeams()`. This is the fan-out `recap.Run` already proves at `internal/recap/recap.go:104`.

**8. Expand `grade` in place; do not add a sibling command.** A second command means a second schedule, Fargate task, run-ledger entry and Infra row, plus a new failure mode ('grade ran but grade-league did not'), and would double-fetch our own team. Mitigations, both required: write my-team rows **before** the league pass starts (not batched at the end), and run the league pass under a context timeout with soft-fail — soft-fail alone covers errors but not hangs. Precedent: `cmd/projection-site.go`'s `renderValueSite` soft-fails independently of the accuracy dashboard deploy.

**9. Ship a paired significance readout, not just bigger numbers.** Without it, 10x rows produce four MAE values that *look* more authoritative while supporting exactly the same conclusions as today. Because all systems project the same player-days, compute the paired difference in absolute error per player-day and emit a confidence interval per slice: 'system X beats Y by N pts/player-day on SP, CI [a,b]'. This is what makes the per-dimension output a decision rather than a leaderboard.

## Non-goals (file separately)

- **Free agents / full player pool.** Leaves waiver-wire projections ungraded.
- **Ensemble / multi-system blending.** The store will hold everything an ensemble needs; evaluating an average or inverse-MAE weighting as a fifth pseudo-system is a follow-up. Do not couple a speculative modeling change to infrastructure that must land first.
- **Per-dimension system selection in production** (e.g. atc-ros for SP, steamer-ros for OF). Requires `BlendSources` to hold multiple simultaneous sources. Depends on this bead — do not commit to acting on a per-slice signal before seeing whether the differences are significant.
- **Blend parameter tuning** (30d window, 250-PA constant, 30%/35% floors, SP 15GP / RP 25GP). The re-gradeable history this bead creates is the prerequisite.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Blend logic exists as one pure function consumed by both `internal/lineuprun` and the grade-time reconstructor; no second implementation of the blend.
- [ ] `grade` writes rows for all 10 fantasy rosters, carrying `FantasyTeamID`, `ProjectedBase` and `DiffBase`; existing partitions are not rewritten.
- [ ] Roster membership per date is point-in-time correct (a mid-window waiver pickup is attributed to the team that held them on that date, not today's holder) — covered by a test.
- [ ] Reconstruction validated against the live snapshot for our own team: per-day drift metric emitted, with a documented tolerance justified by the 10:15am-vs-7:40pm archive/shadow capture gap.
- [ ] My-team rows are committed before the league pass runs; league pass is under a context timeout and soft-fails without losing my-team rows — covered by a test.
- [ ] `report.Model` keyed by `scope|window|role`; the `myteam` scope reproduces today's dashboard numbers exactly (no step change in any existing trend line on ship day).
- [ ] Dashboard exposes a My Team / League toggle with the agreed per-view defaults, and renders a series that starts mid-axis without a false drop to zero.
- [ ] Per-dimension paired comparison shipped: for each (system pair, slice) a paired mean absolute-error difference with a confidence interval. Slices: hitter/pitcher and C/INF/OF/UT/SP/RP.
- [ ] Every position bucket reaches a usable monthly N league-wide (C is the binding constraint at ~15/day vs ~2/day today).
- [ ] Backfill run via existing `grade --dates 2026-07-02:<today>`; no new backfill command. Daily `--window 3` continues to self-heal.
- [ ] `make run-all` passes; `go vet ./...` and `go mod tidy` clean.
notes:
Design settled via /grill-me interview 2026-07-26. Key premise correction recorded in the Problem section: sample size is not the binding constraint on the headline ranking (paired comparison already cancels daily FPts noise) — it is the binding constraint on the per-position slices, which is what this work is actually for. If the top-line ranking barely moves after shipping, that is the expected result, not a failure.

Related: rosterbot-2nd (windowed-recency strategy replay) established the re-gradeable-history pattern this extends. ADR-0002 (team value store accumulates forward) is the contrasting case — that store has no backfill because rosters are not archived; this one does, because `.archive/` holds the FanGraphs inputs and `DailyFantasyPoints` reconstructs historical rosters.

title: Split Fantrax period numbering into WeeklyPeriod/DailyPeriod types
description: Fantrax exposes two unrelated numbering schemes — a weekly matchup axis (ScoringPeriod.Number, ~7 days/period) and a daily roster/apply axis (DailyPeriodFor, one per calendar day) — both represented as a bare int. Nothing at a call site distinguishes them, so a weekly value passed where a daily one is required type-checks silently. This exact bug class caused two production incidents (rosterbot-uv6, rosterbot-z3b) and a third instance is currently open (rosterbot-ren: internal/fantrax/daily_fpts.go uses the naive PeriodForDate instead of the anchored DailyPeriodFor for historical dates).
design: Introduce type WeeklyPeriod int and type DailyPeriod int in internal/fantrax. Update every period-carrying signature to declare its axis: FindCurrentPeriod/FindJustEndedPeriod/GetGSLimits/ScoringPeriod.Number -> WeeklyPeriod; DailyPeriodFor/ApplyLineup/GetHitterRosterForPeriod/GetCurrentPeriod -> DailyPeriod. Thread the types through downstream call sites in internal/lineuprun, internal/gscheck, internal/recap, cmd/backtest.go, cmd/grade.go (~40-50 call sites total, ~20 signatures in internal/fantrax). Go's lack of implicit conversion between named int types means every mismatch becomes a compile error.
acceptance_criteria: All period-carrying function signatures in internal/fantrax use WeeklyPeriod or DailyPeriod instead of bare int. go build and go vet pass. daily_fpts.go's naive PeriodForDate usage is migrated to the anchored DailyPeriodFor or explicitly documented as the accepted rosterbot-ren gap.
close_reason: WeeklyPeriod/DailyPeriod type split landed; historical FP/GS walks now resolve dates via the authoritative periodList map (dailyPeriodForDate). Class-A unification deferred to rosterbot-2ax.

title: GS-check false whole-league Under-Min alert: GetTeamGS used weekly period numbering for daily snapshot diff
description:
## Symptom
On 2026-07-13 the daily gs-check Pushover alert reported '10 violation(s) · max 12, min 10' with ALL 10 teams 'Under Min' at 0–5 GS — for a completed normal week (period 15, 07-06..07-12). No real team starts only 0–5 pitchers in a week whose min is 10.

## Root cause
GetTeamGS reconstructs per-day GS by diffing consecutive DAILY YTD roster snapshots; getPlayerGSSnapshotForPeriod is keyed by the daily scoring period (one number per calendar day, e.g. 104..110 across a week). Commit 92ed478 (rosterbot-uv6) routed the day-walk through fantrax.ResolvePeriod, whose tier-1 (FindCurrentPeriod over the weekly SCHEDULE periods) returns the WEEKLY matchup number (15) for every day in the week. So every day fetched the same daily snapshot #15 (mid-April!), all day-over-day deltas collapsed to 0, and each team's weekly GS under-counted to ~one day's worth (0–5). The limits (min 10/max 12) were correct; the tallies were broken.

Verified live: fixed GetTeamGS yields realistic period-15 tallies (8–13 GS; only 2 teams genuinely under min), vs the broken 0–5.

## Fix (this issue)
Reverted GetTeamGS's walk + baseline to DAILY numbering via gsPeriodWalk/dailyPeriodFor (AnchorPeriodForDate anchored on GetCurrentPeriod, else PeriodForDate) — the same daily numbering its working sibling GetTeamPitcherStarts uses. Dropped the unused periods param from GetTeamGS (+2 callers). Rewrote gs_period_walk_test.go to assert daily numbering. The uv6 test asserting [16]x14 encoded the bug and was removed.

## Follow-up (separate)
The uv6 concern was that a merged multi-day WEEKLY period (All-Star break, period 16 = 07-13..07-26) needs care. The daily numbering handles it correctly IF Fantrax's DAILY periods advance one-per-day through the break. That is unvalidated for the future ASB dates. Validate empirically near 2026-07-27 (when period 16 is first gs-checked) that daily periods 111..124 map to 07-13..07-26 without merges; if Fantrax merges daily periods across the break, GetTeamGS/GetTeamPitcherStarts may need the actual daily-period date map. Filed as [[rosterbot-asb-daily-validate]] context.
acceptance_criteria: gs-check reports realistic per-team GS for a completed normal week (tallies near/above the weekly min, not ~0); only teams genuinely below min are flagged. Unit test locks in daily-numbering walk. Live-verified for period 15.
close_reason: Merged in PR #49 (commit 67e4387) — GetTeamGS reverted to daily-period numbering, live-verified for period 15.

title: GetTeamGS mis-derives period number for every day inside a merged multi-day scoring period
description:
internal/fantrax/gs_check.go's GetTeamGS builds a periodFor closure (lines ~176-184) that resolves each day in its walk via AnchorPeriodForDate(today, currentPeriod, d) -- plain day-by-day anchor arithmetic assuming exactly one scoring period per calendar day. But the ScoringPeriod (sp) GetTeamGS is called with can itself be a merged multi-day period: TestFindCurrentPeriod_MergedAllStarBreakPeriod (internal/fantrax/gs_check_test.go) already fixtures this exact case -- period 16 spans 2026-07-13 to 2026-07-26 (14 calendar days under one period number) for the All-Star break. That merged period starts TOMORROW relative to when this issue was filed (2026-07-12).

GetTeamGS backs both internal/gscheck.RunGSCheck (league-wide GS violation detection, gs-check command) and cmd/optimize.go's GS-budget gate (weekly game-start limit awareness, optimize command when GS_TRACKING_ENABLED=true) -- both live production paths. There is no existing test coverage for GetTeamGS's walk across a merged period.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Use the periods fixture from TestFindCurrentPeriod_MergedAllStarBreakPeriod: period 16 spans StartDate=2026-07-13, EndDate=2026-07-26; period 17 starts 2026-07-27.
2. Call GetTeamGS with sp=period 16 (the merged period), today=2026-07-27 (the day after it ends), and a GetCurrentPeriod() result of 17 (so periodFor uses AnchorPeriodForDate(2026-07-27, 17, d) for each day d in the walk).
3. Observe periodFor(2026-07-13) = 17 + (13-27) = 3, periodFor(2026-07-14) = 4, periodFor(2026-07-20) = 10, periodFor(2026-07-25) = 15 -- all wrong; only periodFor(2026-07-26) = 16 (the day nearest the anchor) happens to be correct.
4. Each wrong period number is a real period elsewhere in the season (e.g. period 3 is an actual April date), so getPlayerGSSnapshotForPeriod(teamID, period) silently returns a real but unrelated day's roster/GS snapshot instead of erroring -- the corruption is silent, not a crash.
design: Thread the already-fetched periods []ScoringPeriod list into GetTeamGS (both callers -- gscheck.go and cmd/optimize.go's GS-budget block -- already have it in scope after rosterbot-z3b) and replace the periodFor closure's AnchorPeriodForDate/PeriodForDate pair with fantrax.ResolvePeriod(periods, currentPeriod, seasonStart, today, d) -- the same periods-list-first resolver rosterbot-z3b introduced for the apply path. This requires changing GetTeamGS's signature to accept periods (or a resolver function) as a parameter.
acceptance_criteria: A test using the existing TestFindCurrentPeriod_MergedAllStarBreakPeriod-style fixture (period 16 spanning multiple calendar days) verifies GetTeamGS's day-by-day walk resolves every day in the merged span to the correct period number, not just the day nearest the anchor. Both GetTeamGS callers (gscheck.RunGSCheck, cmd/optimize.go's GS-budget block) pass their already-fetched periods list through. Existing GetTeamGS tests continue to pass.
notes: Discovered by code-reviewer subagent during rosterbot-z3b's review (2026-07-12), not part of that issue's original scope -- filed separately per reviewer recommendation given the time-sensitivity (this season's period 16 merge starts 2026-07-13, the day after filing).
close_reason: gsPeriodWalk resolves the merged-period walk via ResolvePeriod; code-reviewed, tested, shipped ahead of period 16 opening 2026-07-13.

title: Validate whether hitter/pitcher YTD blend beats a bounded window or no-blend baseline
description:
Two independent audit agents (fantasy-baseball-model-auditor and fantasy-baseball-strategist, 2026-07-10) independently flagged the same risk: internal/projections/blended.go and pitcher_blended.go blend the base FanGraphs RoS projection (depthcharts-ros, which already incorporates 2026 YTD performance with proper regression) with RAW, unregressed season-to-date FP/G. At ~90 GP for a regular, seasonWeight=approxPA/(approxPA+250) is already ~58%. This risks double-counting the same in-season signal and over-reacting to hot/cold streaks.

I extended cmd/backtest.go's --recency-experiment harness (previously ytd/w14/w30/decay21 only) with a 'base' variant (no blend at all, pure depthcharts-ros) to isolate the effect, and ran it live:

  --matchup (last completed week, 2026-06-29..2026-07-05, 7 days):
    base    realized=387.0  meanGap=-19.14
    ytd     realized=405.0  meanGap=-16.57  (current production strategy — WON this week)
    w14     realized=340.0  meanGap=-25.86
    w30     realized=396.0  meanGap=-17.86
    decay21 realized=389.0  meanGap=-18.86

  --weeks 4 (2026-06-15..2026-07-09, 25 days):
    base    realized=1252.0 meanGap=-23.76
    ytd     realized=1226.0 meanGap=-24.80  (current production strategy — worse than base AND w30)
    w14     realized=1151.0 meanGap=-27.80  (clearly worst)
    w30     realized=1261.0 meanGap=-23.40  (best of all 5 variants)
    decay21 realized=1217.0 meanGap=-25.16

Over the longer window, current production (ytd/season-to-date) is beaten by both a bounded 30-day window AND a no-blend baseline. The single-week result flips the other way, consistent with a real-but-modest, sample-dependent effect rather than a huge bug. 25 hitter-days is still a small sample for a strategy decision that affects every lineup every day.
acceptance_criteria: Run --recency-experiment over a much longer window (full season to date, or --weeks 8+) to get a stable read. If w30 (or base) continues to beat ytd, either (a) switch BlendedSource's recent-stats input from unbounded season-to-date to a bounded rolling window, or (b) blend against a preseason (independent) projection instead of an in-season-updated RoS system, or (c) lower the recent-weight ceiling. Extend the same experiment to pitchers (pitcher_blended.go) — the current harness is hitters-only. Update CLAUDE.md's Blended scoring section once a decision is made.
notes: Tooling change (the 'base' variant + HasProjDiag n/a-vs-0.00 fix in internal/backtest/strategy_replay.go and cmd/backtest.go) already committed. This issue is about acting on what the tool shows, not about the tool itself.
close_reason: Shipped: internal/lineuprun/recent.go windowedHitterRecent + projections.WindowWeight(30) live; w30-beats-YTD decision + pitchers-stay-YTD recorded in CLAUDE.md Blended scoring section.

comments.text:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Determine whether the production hitter/pitcher recent-performance blend is actually improving lineup decisions versus simpler alternatives, and act on the finding.

**Current behavior:**
The blend combines the season-long base projection with the player's raw season-to-date performance, weighted increasingly toward recent performance as the season progresses. A strategy-comparison tool exists that can replay several alternative strategies (no blend at all, various rolling windows) against actual historical lineup outcomes. A short initial comparison run showed the current strategy losing to both a no-blend baseline and a bounded 30-day window over a 4-week sample, but winning over a single-week sample — not enough data to be confident either way.

**Desired behavior:**
A confident, data-backed answer on whether the current blend strategy is the best of the available options for both hitters and pitchers, backed by a much larger sample than what's been checked so far, followed by either confirming the current approach or switching to whichever alternative the data supports.

**Key interfaces:**
- The existing strategy-comparison tool already supports adding/removing named strategies to compare; extending it to pitchers (currently hitters-only) is straightforward if needed.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] The comparison has been run over a much larger sample (full season to date at minimum) for hitters.
- [ ] A decision has been made and recorded: keep the current strategy, or switch to a specific alternative, with the reasoning captured.
- [ ] If a change is made, it's verified not to regress recent lineup outcomes before being treated as the new default.

**Why this needs a human, not an agent:**
This changes a formula that determines every lineup's point projections, every day, for the rest of the season — a live, standing decision with real competitive stakes, not a self-contained bug fix. "How much data is enough to be confident" and "which alternative to prefer if several look close" are judgment calls the maintainer should make directly rather than delegate. An agent CAN be asked to do the mechanical part (re-run the comparison tool over a longer window and report the numbers back) as a preliminary, lower-stakes step if useful — that sub-task would itself be ready-for-agent even though the decision that follows isn't.

**Out of scope:**
- Changing the blend formula's underlying shrinkage math (the plate-appearance-based weighting curve itself) — that's a separate, deeper design question from "which recency window to blend."

title: Remove GS_MAX/GS_MIN static env vars; source everything live from Fantrax
description: Now that GS budget/gscheck fetch real limits live from Fantrax (rosterbot-r10), the GS_MAX/GS_MIN numeric env vars only ever served as a fallback value + feature toggle. Replace with a single GS_TRACKING_ENABLED boolean toggle; on live-fetch failure, send a Pushover alert (PUSHOVER_USER_KEY) instead of falling back to a stale static number. Also remove GS_MAX/GS_MIN from infra/infra.go's ECS secrets and the AWS SSM parameters. Discovered along the way: internal/lineupapi (used by the Lambda in lambda/) transitively imports internal/fantrax, and lambda/go.mod had no replace pin for the go-fantrax fork branch, so cdk synth was already broken on main since PR #29 merged — fixed as part of this work.

See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-06-fantrax-gs-limits-design.md.

Follow-up rosterbot-6ds tracks post-merge go.mod cleanup.

title: GS gate: fractional tail mixes value with count, and certaintyMargin is an order of magnitude too small
description: internal/optimizer/gs_budget.go. (1) Units: at :196 the fractional tail entry is 'placeholder * weight' where weight is a fractional COUNT (<=1), making it an expectation (value x probability), while every other entry in the ranking is a per-start value in points — and the cut at :224 spends a WHOLE slot on it. The trigger at :130 counts estimated demand fractionally but the allocation spends whole slots, so the fractional tail systematically loses the cut and future demand is under-reserved. This is an overcorrection of an earlier bug where the tail was ceil-rounded to full value; the fix swung past the target. Correct form is to keep the entry at full placeholder value and make the budget fractional, or to use one fractional currency throughout. (2) certaintyMargin=0.10 at :171 requires an estimated future start to beat today's by only 10% before outranking it, but measured SP projection MAE is 10.4-13.8 FP/game against an SP projection mean around 12 — projection noise on a single start is ~100% of its mean, so a 10% haircut is an order of magnitude too tight to encode 'this start might not happen at all'. Together with rosterbot-abd, all three defects push the same direction: under-reserving budget for future starts. In a weekly-capped league that means spending GS on Monday/Tuesday arms and hitting the cap before a Saturday ace — same number of starts, worse ones. The value-ranked pooling design itself is correct and should be kept; only the estimation and pricing of future demand is wrong.
acceptance_criteria: Trigger and allocation use one consistent currency. certaintyMargin re-derived from measured SP projection dispersion rather than left at 0.10.

title: Hourly optimize is 64% no-op and 75% of applied moves are re-flips
description: Measured from all notification objects in the state bucket: 711 kind=lineup notifications originate from only 224 distinct run_ids out of 613 optimize runs, so ~36% of hourly runs change anything. Of the moves that do apply, ~75% are re-flips of a (target_date, player) pair already moved — Alec Bohm was flipped 32 times for target date 2026-07-21 alone, Ryan Jeffers 29, Taylor Ward 29. Only ~16% of notifications concern today; 84% are future-dated --matchup speculation that gets re-decided next hour. 14% of changes gain <0.5 projected pts and 19% gain <1.0, which is far inside the 4.38 hitter MAE — i.e. the bot is applying and notifying on differences it cannot actually resolve. The zeroGainEps=1e-9 guard only catches exactly-zero gain.
design: Two changes, both cheap: (a) a real minimum-gain threshold (~1.0-1.5 projected pts, inside measured MAE) instead of zeroGainEps; (b) restrict the hourly loop to today only, and run the --matchup future pass once daily. Today is the only thing an hourly cadence can legitimately learn new information about (scratches, probables); re-deciding Saturday's lineup every hour on Tuesday is pure churn.
acceptance_criteria: Lineup churn and Pushover volume drop substantially without losing same-day late-scratch responsiveness.

title: System comparison ranks on unequal samples and pools LegacySystem into the incumbent
description: Two defects in internal/report make the dashboard's 'Best' system flag untrustworthy. (1) LegacySystem pooling: Aggregate attributes every empty-System row to detailSystem (depthcharts-ros). Verified from the raw store: LEGACY is MAE 4.8915 over n=298 across 14 days (2026-06-16..06-29, BEFORE any shadow system existed) while depthcharts-ros proper is MAE 4.9989 over n=552 across 27 days; pooling reports 4.9612. The incumbent is credited with 14 easier days no challenger was allowed to compete on, and on the true common window it ranks 3rd of 4 rather than 2nd. (2) rankSystems filters each system's rows independently and never intersects them, guarding only on N>0 — coverage is 40/25/25/22 days and n=827/509/509/439. A paired comparison on the 439-row intersection does show steamer-ros beating depthcharts-ros by 0.072 pts/player-day (p<0.001), but that is ~1.5% of MAE against within-day rank skill of +0.12, so it will flip almost no start/bench decisions. Do NOT switch production systems on this evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Compare/rankSystems inner-joins on (dt, player_id) across compared systems and reports the intersection N. LegacySystem rows are excluded from comparison (retained in detail Views for history). Best is set only when a paired test clears a minimum-N gate.

title: GS forecast caps pitcher count by slot count before dividing by rotation size
description: internal/lineuprun/gsbudget.go: the unannounced-day branch computes spPlaying (a count of rostered SPs whose team plays), caps it at numPSlots (a count of active pitcher SLOTS), then divides by rotationSize to get df.Estimated. The cap is applied to the wrong quantity — what is bounded by slot count is STARTS, not pitchers-whose-team-plays. Correct form is min(spPlaying/rotationSize, numPSlots). The branch immediately above it caps df.ConfirmedStarters at numPSlots, which IS correct because those are already starts — the contrast makes the unit error clear. Measured against the real roster (10 rostered SPs, 6 active pitcher slots): at 7 SPs playing Estimated=1.20 vs correct 1.40; at 8, 1.20 vs 1.60; at 10, 1.20 vs 2.00. With 10 rostered SPs the cap binds nearly every day, understating each unannounced day by 0.2-0.8 starts.
acceptance_criteria: Estimated future starts are not understated when more rostered SPs have a game than there are pitcher slots. Unit test covering spPlaying > numPSlots.

title: Recap site viewership metrics: who is reading the weekly recap and how much
description:
No visibility into whether anyone reads the weekly recap. The recap site is built by recap-site into dist/, synced to SITE_BUCKET, and served by the SiteCdn CloudFront distribution (infra/infra.go). It is fully public: no auth, no signed URLs, no viewer-request function -- and CloudFront access logging is NOT enabled on the distribution today, so there is currently no signal at all, not even raw hits.

Scope is the recap site ONLY. The dashboard SPA and the lineup API are explicitly out of scope.

Want to answer: is anyone opening the weekly recap, which weeks get read (just the latest, or do people browse back through week-NN.html), and does readership hold up over the season or decay after the novelty. That last one is the decision this feeds: recap-site rebuilds every completed week on a schedule, and if nobody is reading it that cost is not justified.

Constraint that shapes everything: the page is public and the audience is a ~12-person league sharing one link. There is no login to attribute a view to, so 'who' is not directly answerable the way it would be on the passkey-gated dashboard.
design:
DECIDED 2026-07-27. Two steps; step 1 is shipped in PR #91.

STEP 1 (done, PR #91): enable CloudFront standard logging on SiteCdn -> RecapLogBucket under recap/, 90-day expiry, ObjectOwnership=OBJECT_WRITER (CloudFront logs via ACL; the CDK default silently yields no logs). Glue table rosterbot_analysis.recap_access_logs for ad-hoc queries. DashboardCdn deliberately not logged.

STEP 2 (this issue, blocked on step 1 being DEPLOYED so real log objects exist): surface it on the dashboard SPA.

  Data path -- read the log objects from S3 directly. NOT Athena. A pure aggregator walks the recap/ prefix with internal/s3blob (Walk + Get, from rosterbot-oye), gunzips, parses the TSV, and produces a Model. This matches internal/report and internal/valuereport exactly -- pure aggregation, no I/O in the domain package, serialized straight to JSON. Athena was rejected: it adds the Athena SDK, async submit/poll, and reading results back out of S3 -- three independently-failing moving parts for a dataset small enough to read whole. The 90-day lifecycle rule bounds the scan for free.

  Content -- a RECENT HITS TABLE only. Columns: timestamp (log_date + log_time, UTC), client IP, page (uri_stem), edge location. This is the literal ask -- when, and from what IP. Explicitly NOT building: views-over-time chart, per-week-page breakdown, distinct-readers-per-day. Do not add them speculatively.

  Wiring -- follow the model.json/value.json path exactly: written by projection-site (or its own command) to ./report/views.json, synced by entrypoint.sh under DASHBOARD_BUCKET's report/ prefix, fetched client-side by a new SPA tab. Soft-fail independently like renderValueSite does, so a log-parsing hiccup never blocks the accuracy dashboard deploy.

  Filtering -- restrict to real page reads (status 200, uri_stem LIKE '%.html') so CSS/asset/favicon requests do not drown the table. CloudFront logs every object, not every page view.

  Geolocation -- edge_location only (the POP that served the request, e.g. SFO5 -> rough metro). Standard logs carry no country field; real geo needs standard logging v2 or an IP->geo lookup. Confirmed nice-to-have, not required. Do not add a dependency for it.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A dashboard SPA tab shows a recent-hits table for the recap site: timestamp, client IP, page, edge location.
2. Rows are real page reads -- status 200 and .html only, not every asset request.
3. views.json is produced by a pure aggregator with no I/O in the domain package, reading log objects via internal/s3blob; no Athena SDK dependency is added.
4. A failure to read or parse logs soft-fails and does not block model.json/value.json publication.
5. Empty state renders cleanly -- a freshly deployed log prefix has no objects, and the tab must not error on that.
6. Documented in CLAUDE.md alongside the other dashboard/report sections.
notes:
Step 1 shipped as PR #91 (branch feat/recap-access-logs) on 2026-07-27; NOT yet merged/deployed at time of writing. Step 2 is blocked until it deploys and real log objects accumulate -- building the renderer against an empty prefix means 'verifying' it against nothing.

Also depends on rosterbot-oye (PR #90) merging, since the aggregator reads via internal/s3blob.

Scope was narrowed twice by the user: first from three surfaces (dashboard SPA + recap site + lineup API) to the recap site ONLY, then from four candidate visualizations to the recent-hits table ONLY.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #91 (ed881cb: CloudFront standard logging on SiteCdn -> RecapLogBucket under recap/, 90-day expiry, Glue table) and PR #92 (dcdfd8b: Views tab + internal/recaplog aggregator), both merged to main. All 6 acceptance criteria verified against main: (1) web/dashboard/views.js renders the recent-hits table, tab wired at index.html:38; (2) recaplog.IsPageRead filters to status 200 + / or *.html; (3) pure aggregator reading via internal/s3blob, no Athena SDK in go.mod; (4) renderViewsSite soft-fails with a warning (cmd/projection-site.go:87) and never blocks model.json/value.json; (5) empty prefix renders 'No page reads recorded yet.' (views.js:98); (6) CLAUDE.md documents internal/recaplog. go test ./internal/recaplog/... passes.

title: Infra tab: AWS data-state status page on the dashboard
description:
Add an 'Infra' tab to the dashboard SPA (web/dashboard/) showing the health and freshness of every durable and ephemeral data artifact in AWS, so "is anything quietly broken?" is one glance instead of an S3 spelunk.

TODAY there is no way to see this. The Jobs and Runs tabs answer "did the job run?" — they read the run ledger. They do NOT answer "did the job produce data, and is that data still arriving?" A job can exit 0 having written nothing, and nothing surfaces it. Two failure modes make that more than cosmetic:

1. The Team Value Store ACCUMULATES FORWARD AND CANNOT BE BACKFILLED (docs/adr/0002). HKB has no history and rosters are not archived, so a day missed is permanently lost. A silent gap in analysis/team-values/dt=* is unrecoverable data loss that currently nobody would notice until the Value tab's chart looked wrong.
2. The Analysis Store partitions by dt AND system (4 shadow systems). A shadow capture that silently stops for one system degrades the model-comparison ranking without any error anywhere.

WHAT TO SURFACE — every artifact, its last-written partition/date, its age, and a health verdict:

  Durable (S3, keep-forever):
    analysis/grades/dt=*/system=*   Analysis Store — last dt, size, and WHICH of the 4 systems reported (a missing system is the interesting case)
    analysis/team-values/dt=*       Team Value Store — last dt + GAP DETECTION across the series (see above; gaps are permanent)
    archive/<source>/dt=*           daily raw-data archive — per source: hkb, fangraphs (4 systems x bat/pit = 8 blobs), savant (5 CSVs), prospects
    backtest/snapshots/             flat per-day projection snapshots (what the "backtest" command grades)
    backtest/snapshots-systems/     per-system shadow captures
    runledger/, runs/, notifications/, lineup/, claims/, session/

  Ephemeral (TTL-evicted, regenerable):
    cache/                          total size, object count, and age distribution by TTL tier (todayTTL 15m / stableTTL 7d / pastPeriodTTL 30d) — plus the provider-specific ones: fangraphs 24h, savant 24h, hkb 8h, prospect-rankings 168h

  Producers: map each artifact to the EventBridge schedule that writes it (Lineup, Prospects, GsCheck, Waivers, Transactions, Claims, Backtest, Grade, ProjectionSite, Archive, TeamValues, Shadow) so a stale artifact points at a suspect job.
design:
TWO PLAUSIBLE DATA PATHS — pick deliberately, they have different properties:

  (a) PRECOMPUTED JSON, like the existing Projections and Value tabs. A command (extend the "projection-site" command, or add a new "infra-status" one) walks the prefixes, writes report/infra.json under DASHBOARD_BUCKET, and infra.js fetches it. Cheap, no new IAM, no new API surface, matches the two newest tabs. But it is only as fresh as its last scheduled run — a real weakness for a page whose entire job is detecting staleness. A status page that is itself stale can report "all healthy" while the producer that writes it is the thing that died.

  (b) LIVE API, like Jobs/Runs. New GET /v1/infra route in internal/lineupapi doing the S3 listing on demand. Always current, and it can honestly report its own failure. Costs a new route, Lambda S3 list permissions across the prefixes, and latency (many ListObjectsV2 calls) — mitigable with a short server-side cache.

RECOMMEND (b) for correctness of purpose, with a small TTL. If (a) is chosen for expedience, the page MUST prominently display the generated-at timestamp of infra.json itself and go red when that is stale — otherwise the page can lie in exactly the situation it exists to catch.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES:
- Prefix layout is already centralized in internal/statestore (artifact{s3Prefix, localDir}). Read it from there; do NOT hardcode a second copy of the prefix table — that is precisely what rosterbot-9s6 collapsed.
- Prefer S3 ListObjectsV2 with delimiter to enumerate dt= partitions without fetching objects. Row counts, if shown, need object reads — consider showing object SIZE instead, which listing gives free.
- Health thresholds should be per-artifact, not global: cache/ being 15 minutes old is healthy; analysis/team-values/ being 2 days old is not. Encode the expected cadence per artifact alongside the prefix.
- Follow the existing SPA conventions: add a route to ROUTES in app.js, a nav anchor href="#infra" in index.html, and an infra.js exporting renderInfra(root). Vendored Chart.js is already available if a sparkline of arrival history is wanted.
- The dashboard is passkey-gated; the precomputed JSON files are NOT (documented in docs/aws-deployment.md). If (a) is chosen, infra.json inherits that same public-by-URL exposure — check nothing sensitive (bucket names, ARNs, account IDs) lands in it.
acceptance_criteria:
1. An 'Infra' tab exists in the dashboard nav and routes to a rendered view.
2. Every durable prefix and the ephemeral cache are listed with last-written date, age, and a health verdict.
3. Team Value Store gap detection is present and calls out missing days explicitly — this is the artifact that cannot be backfilled.
4. Analysis Store shows per-system coverage, so one shadow system silently stopping is visible.
5. Archive shows per-source freshness (hkb / fangraphs / savant / prospects), not one aggregate.
6. Each artifact names the EventBridge schedule that produces it.
7. The page cannot silently present stale data as healthy: either it reads live, or it displays and alarms on its own generation timestamp.
8. Prefix layout is read from internal/statestore, not duplicated.
9. Works in both light and dark, and on a phone — this is a page to check from bed when a Pushover fires.
notes: Requested 2026-07-25. Related: the Jobs and Runs tabs already cover run-level status via the run ledger; this is deliberately the DATA-level complement and should not duplicate them. Consider cross-linking a stale artifact to its producer job's last run in the Runs tab.
close_reason: Shipped. PR #85, merged as 54359b2. GET /v1/infra + Infra dashboard tab, live S3 listing (not precomputed — a status page built from a scheduled artifact goes stale in exactly the situation it exists to detect). New zero-dep leaf internal/statestore/layout is now the single bucket-layout declaration (statestore imports lineupapi, so lineupapi could never import statestore back). 15 tests, all judgement logic testable without AWS. Gap detection scans only to yesterday (today's producer may not have run) and is fatal only where NoBackfill is set. Sub-dimension coverage surfaces a stopped shadow system as a missing chip. IAM = s3:ListBucket only, never GetObject. Verified live against local state: correctly flagged a 12-day-old Fantrax session cookie as stale. UI screenshotted light/dark/390px + synthetic gap fixture. Extra beyond issue scope: lineupapi.NewFileInfraStore so local serve shows the same view (needed to verify UI at all — SPA is passkey-gated).

title: Add a LICENSE to the public repo
description:
github.com/nixon-commits/rosterbot is PUBLIC and has NO license file (confirmed via gh repo view: visibility=PUBLIC, license=NONE). Under default copyright that means all rights reserved: nobody can legally fork, use, modify or contribute, even though the source is readable. Anyone who has already cloned it is technically in the wrong.

One-file fix that changes the repo's legal posture.
design:
The choice is the owner's call, not a default to be assumed. MIT is the usual pick for a personal project like this and is the least friction.

The repo vendors nothing but depends on github.com/pmurley/go-fantrax and the AWS SDK; neither appears to impose copyleft that would constrain the choice, but confirm before picking.

Add the file, then make sure GitHub picks it up so the license shows in the repo sidebar (it detects standard LICENSE filenames and contents automatically).
acceptance_criteria:
1. A LICENSE file exists at the repo root.
2. GitHub shows the license in the repo sidebar.
notes:
SCOPE REDUCED 2026-07-25: originally also proposed retiring docs/superpowers/ and docs/agents/. Owner decided to KEEP both — do not delete them.

One genuinely stale item was found during that survey and is worth a separate look someday, but is NOT part of this issue: docs/agents/issue-tracker.md describes issues living as markdown under .scratch/<feature-slug>/, a directory that does not exist (the repo uses beads now), and CLAUDE.md:227 still cites it as current. That is a doc-accuracy nit, not a deletion.
close_reason: Added GPL-3.0 LICENSE. NOTE: the issue's design assumption was wrong — go-fantrax (both pmurley upstream and the nixon-commits fork) is GPL-3.0 and is statically linked, so the combined work must be GPL-3.0; MIT was not available. Owner chose GPL-3.0 after being shown the finding. README gained a License section explaining the constraint.

title: Extract BlendSources phase: make projection blending pure and testable
description:
rosterbot-6rv criterion 3, remaining half. The GS-budget half landed in PR #84 (countTodayStarts pure, buildGSForecast behind a schedule seam, 8 tests). Projection blending did not.

Blending currently happens inline in lineuprun.Run across two blocks — the hitter section (~50 lines, windowedHitterRecent + BlendedSource wiring) and the pitcher section (~90 lines, GetRecentPitcherStats + PitcherBlendedSource). Neither is exercised by any test; windowedHitterRecent in particular reconstructs a per-day FPts series via DailyFantasyPoints over ~35 days and collapses it through projections.WindowedRecent + WindowWeight(30), and a mistake there silently shifts every hitter's Expected Points.

The issue's own design note calls this out: 'GSBudget and BlendSources should come out fully pure; that is where the real leverage is.'
design:
Mirror what worked for the GS-budget extraction: identify the genuinely pure core, put a narrow interface in front of the fetch, and inject anything expensive as a func value rather than passing a whole source.

The pure core is the collapse of a per-day FPts series into per-player FP/game + games-in-window. That should be a function taking the already-fetched []fantrax.DayRoster and returning the recent-stat map, with no client at all. The fetch (DailyFantasyPoints over the trailing window) stays behind the existing recentStatsClient seam.

Pitchers are simpler — GetRecentPitcherStats returns a YTD snapshot map directly — so the phase is mostly about lifting the BlendedSource/PitcherBlendedSource construction and its GP-threshold logic somewhere testable.

Both roles must keep their asymmetry: hitters use a trailing 30-day window (rosterbot-2nd), pitchers use season-to-date YTD. That asymmetry is deliberate and backtest-justified; do not unify it.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Blending logic runs in tests with no network and no credentials.
2. The hitter window collapse is a pure function over already-fetched data.
3. Hitters stay on the 30-day window and pitchers on YTD — the rosterbot-2nd asymmetry is preserved and a test says so.
4. Dry-run output stays byte-identical (build a baseline binary from the pre-change commit; run back-to-back with identical stream redirection — live projections drift within the hour).
notes: Baseline-diff technique and its two gotchas are recorded on rosterbot-6rv.
close_reason: Closed

title: Declare a narrow Fantrax interface in lineuprun, recap and gscheck instead of taking the concrete 34-method client
description:
internal/fantrax.Client exposes 34 methods over roster fetch, period math, scoring config, lineup apply, stats/backfill, player pool, transactions and matchups, and embeds two concrete upstream types with no interface between them (client.go:188 -- public *gofantrax.Client, auth *auth_client.Client).

Three consumer packages take that concrete client as their entry-point parameter:
  internal/lineuprun/lineuprun.go:130   Run(ft *fantrax.Client, cfg *config.Config, opts Options)

title: DailyFantasyPoints leaks NeedsBackfill to callers; recap seasonToDateTeamMean skips the backfill and undercounts
description:
internal/fantrax.DailyFantasyPoints (daily_fpts.go:70) zeroes a player deltaFP/deltaGP on first appearance in the window and on a two-way role crossing, flags the row NeedsBackfill (daily_fpts.go:34), and returns it as-is. Resolving those placeholders requires a SECOND, separate call to Client.BackfillDailyFPts (mlb_backfill.go:81), which fetches the MLB statsapi game log and scores it via the Scoring Weights.

That pairing is a convention, not an invariant. Six call sites exist; five remember it, one does not:

  PAIRED:   cmd/grade.go:65+69, cmd/backtest.go:96+100, cmd/backtest.go:172+176,
            internal/recap/recap.go:245+249, internal/lineuprun/recent.go:47+53
  UNPAIRED: internal/recap/recap.go:555 (seasonToDateTeamMean)

seasonToDateTeamMean fetches the full seasonStart..asOf window and hands the rows straight to computeSeasonMeanFromDays (recap.go:559), which cannot distinguish a placeholder zero from a genuine off-day. Every player whose first appearance falls mid-window -- i.e. every mid-season waiver pickup and every Ohtani-style role crossing -- contributes 0 FPts on that day, silently deflating the teams season-to-date daily mean. That mean feeds the recap win-probability model via fetchSeasonMeans, so the error propagates into the WP curves and Game of the Week pick.

This is the interface defect behind the bug: NeedsBackfill is an implementation detail (Fantrax YTD snapshot diffs cannot see a players first appearance) promoted onto the interface as a flag callers must remember to act on.

Surfaced by the 2026-07-22 architecture review (candidate 3 of 7, top recommendation).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Pick a team that acquired a player via waivers or trade mid-season, and a week after that acquisition.
2. Run: go run . recap --dates <that week> --out /tmp/recap.html
3. Instrument or inspect seasonToDateTeamMean (internal/recap/recap.go:551) for that teamID -- note the DayPlayerFP rows where NeedsBackfill is true and FPts is 0.
4. Compare the returned mean against the same computation with ft.BackfillDailyFPts(days) inserted after recap.go:555.
5. The unpatched mean is lower; the gap scales with how many rostered players first appear mid-window.
design:
Deepen the module rather than adding a sixth reminder to call the pairing.

Move the backfill inside DailyFantasyPoints so the returned []DayRoster never contains placeholder zeros:
  - DailyFantasyPoints resolves NeedsBackfill rows internally before returning.
  - BackfillDailyFPts becomes unexported (backfillDailyFPts); the five paired call sites drop their explicit call and their error-handling block.
  - NeedsBackfill stays on the struct only if some caller genuinely needs to know a row was reconstructed rather than diffed; otherwise it becomes unexported too.

Error policy must be decided explicitly and documented on DailyFantasyPoints: the existing backfill soft-fails to leave-zero on any MLB statsapi error, and internal/lineuprun/recent.go:53 already discards the error outright (_ = ft.BackfillDailyFPts(days)). Preserve soft-fail so a statsapi hiccup never breaks a recap, but the behaviour belongs in the doc comment as part of the interface, not in five call sites.

Cost note: the backfill is bounded to a handful of statsapi calls per window and is already paid by five of six callers, so folding it in does not change the network profile of any existing paired path. seasonToDateTeamMean (a full-season window) is the one path that gains calls -- it is also the one currently producing wrong numbers.
acceptance_criteria:
1. internal/recap/recap.go:555 (seasonToDateTeamMean) no longer returns placeholder zeros for mid-window first appearances.
2. DailyFantasyPoints resolves the backfill internally; BackfillDailyFPts is no longer exported.
3. The five previously-paired call sites (grade.go, backtest.go x2, recap.go:245, recent.go) call DailyFantasyPoints alone and still produce identical output.
4. A unit test covers the mid-window-first-appearance case and the two-way role-crossing case through the DailyFantasyPoints interface (not through the unexported backfill).
5. The soft-fail-on-statsapi-error policy is documented on DailyFantasyPoints doc comment.
6. Recap totals still match the Fantrax-authoritative Matchup.HomeTeam.Points for a spot-checked week (the existing verification described in CLAUDE.md).
7. go vet ./... and make test pass; CLAUDE.md updated where it describes the DailyFantasyPoints/BackfillDailyFPts pairing.
close_reason: Folded MLB-statsapi backfill into DailyFantasyPoints; backfillDailyFPts + needsBackfill unexported; seasonToDateTeamMean (WP-model input) now backfills. Covered by TestDailyFantasyPoints_ResolvesBackfillInternally via a fetchPeriodSnapshotFn seam.

title: optimize: blank player names in lineup-change notifications for future dates
description:
## Symptom
Fantrax Lineup Pushover alerts for future dates (seen during the All-Star-break --matchup run, e.g. Jul 23/25/26) show pitcher/hitter moves with MISSING names — 'arrow -> P' and 'arrow -> BN' with no player name — while other moves render fine.

## Root cause
cmd/optimize.go builds the change-line name lookup (playerName map) ONCE from today's base roster (GetHitterRoster/GetPitcherRoster). But the per-date apply loop optimizes future dates against PERIOD-SPECIFIC rosters (GetHitterRosterForPeriod/GetPitcherRosterForPeriod), which can include players not on today's active roster (e.g. reserve/IL SPs surfaced for a matchup week). When the optimizer activates or benches such a player, playerName[id] is empty -> blank name in the notification. Verified live: today's base pitcher roster = 14, period rosters = 20; 8 pitcher IDs (Griffin Jax, Dennis Santana, Yusei Kikuchi, ...) are absent from the base map. Not merged-period-specific and not caused by the GS fix (rosterbot-wd5); a latent bug surfaced by multi-future-date --matchup optimization.

## Fix
Resolve change-line names from THIS date's result (dr.hitterResult/pitcherResult .Scored players carry the period-specific names), seeded from the global map for safety. Applied to both stdout change list and the Pushover summary. Live-verified: 2026-07-26 now shows 'Griffin Jax -> P', 'Dennis Santana -> P', etc.; also fixed blank '-> BN -0.00' cosmetic moves (Joey Wiemer, Julio Rodriguez).
acceptance_criteria: Future-date optimize runs render all activated/benched player names in stdout and Pushover output, including players present only in the period-specific roster. Live-verified for 2026-07-26 and 2026-07-28.
close_reason: Merged in PR #51 (commit ca41337) — change-line names now resolved from the period-specific optimizer result, live-verified for 2026-07-26/28.

title: Validate daily-period numbering across the All-Star break (period 16) for GS tally
description:
Follow-up to rosterbot-wd5. GetTeamGS/GetTeamPitcherStarts walk the merged 2-week ASB period (16, 2026-07-13..07-26) using daily anchor arithmetic, which assumes Fantrax's DAILY scoring periods advance one-per-calendar-day through the break. If Fantrax merges daily periods during the break (as it merges the WEEKLY matchup period), the anchor arithmetic drifts and the per-day snapshot diff could mis-attribute a start or two around the break boundary. Impact is small (few games during the break) but should be confirmed.

## What to do
Near/after 2026-07-27 (first gs-check of period 16), run the gs-check dry-run (or a probe) and confirm: (a) daily periods 111..124 actually map to 07-13..07-26 with no merges, and (b) the period-16 GS tallies are realistic. If daily periods DO merge across the break, the walk needs Fantrax's authoritative daily-period date map rather than pure anchor arithmetic — coordinate with the still-open rosterbot-ren (exact date→period map).
acceptance_criteria: Confirmed whether Fantrax daily periods merge across the ASB; period-16 GS tallies validated as correct, or a follow-up fix filed if they drift.
close_reason: Superseded by rosterbot-2ax (closed 2026-07-16). The ASB-drift risk this was meant to validate is structurally eliminated: gsPeriodWalk->DailyPeriodFor now resolves each day via the authoritative periodDateMap (Fantrax periodList date->daily-period dropdown) first, not pure anchor arithmetic — so any daily-period merge/insertion across the All-Star break is reflected automatically. Both deps (rosterbot-ren, rosterbot-2ax) landed. No manual 07-27 probe needed.

title: Team HKB dynasty-value tracker on projection-site (value.html)
description:
Add a daily-accumulating time-series of each fantasy team's aggregate HKB dynasty value, rendered as a new value.html page on the projection-site, with a team multi-select and a metric selector that breaks value out by MLB vs minors and hitter vs pitcher.

## Why
Nothing today trends roster/farm value over time. HKB gives each player an integer Value (dynasty), and GetFullPlayerPool exposes every team's players with a MinorsEligible flag, so per-team aggregates are a cheap join we already have all inputs for. This surfaces who is accumulating value via trades/waivers and whose farm is strengthening.

## Hard constraint (shapes the whole design)
HKB serves ONLY current values (no history), and the durable archive never stores fantasy rosters. Past team compositions cannot be reconstructed. Therefore the series MUST accumulate forward: compute today's per-team aggregate each day and append to a durable store. Cold-start = begin today (2026-07-12), grow one point/day; no counterfactual backfill.

## Resolved design (from grill-me session 2026-07-12)
- Location: projection-site, as a SEPARATE value.html file cross-linked from index.html (report.Model/template untouched).
- Metric: HKB Value summed over rostered players (FantasyTeamID != ""), joined by normalized name (same join as internal/claims + internal/transactions). Unmatched players contribute 0; store rostered vs matched counts for join-coverage transparency.
- Stored as 4 leaf cells per (date, team): hitter/pitcher x MLB/minors. Render derives Total / MLB / Minors / Hitter / Pitcher toggles.
- Minors = Fantrax MinorsEligible (from the single GetFullPlayerPool call; zero extra cost).
- Store: new internal/teamvalue package mirroring internal/analysis (Analysis Store) - date-partitioned NDJSON, isolated s3teamvalue adapter, glob-reader, re-run safe. Team name + logo DENORMALIZED into each row (from GetScoringPeriodsAndTeams) so value.html render needs zero Fantrax calls.
- Producer: new 'team-values' command, own EventBridge schedule ~14:00 UTC (before projection-site's 15:00 UTC). Keeps projection-site a pure read+render step (no Fantrax auth dependency).
- UI: one multi-team time plot, team multi-select + metric selector; minors breakout = the Minors line.

## Acceptance
- team-values command writes today's per-team NDJSON partition (local .teamvalue when STATE_BUCKET unset, S3 analysis/team-values/ prefix when set).
- projection-site emits value.html with a working multi-team time plot + team & metric selectors, reading the teamvalue store; self-contained (Chart.js, inline data).
- EventBridge schedule runs team-values daily before projection-site; CLAUDE.md + README + Makefile run-all updated.

## Child slices
1. internal/teamvalue store package (schema + NDJSON + FileWriter/FileReader)
2. teamvalue aggregation logic (HKB x pool join, bucketing) - pure, unit-tested
3. internal/teamvalue/s3teamvalue adapter (mirror s3grades)
4. cmd/team-values.go command + Makefile run-all + README
5. value.html render (Chart.js multi-line, selectors)
6. projection-site wiring to emit value.html
7. CDK team-values EventBridge schedule
8. Docs: CLAUDE.md architecture entry + short ADR (accumulate-forward, MinorsEligible split)
close_reason: All 8 slices delivered: teamvalue store + s3 adapter + aggregation, team-values command, valuereport render (browser-verified), projection-site value.html wiring, CDK TeamValues schedule, docs+ADR. Full build/vet/test green.

title: Consolidate period resolution into one Period Resolver module
description: Four independent derivations of "what scoring period is date X" exist with no single module owning the answer: PeriodForDate (season-start day math), AnchorPeriodForDate (anchor on todays current period), GetMatchupWeekNumberForDate (positional count over matchupWeekRanges, no gap check) in internal/fantrax/matchup_weeks.go, and period.Number parsed directly from Fantrax caption text in internal/gscheck. cmd/optimize.go and internal/gscheck each pick their own derivation for the GS-budget block. Architecture review (improve-codebase-architecture, 2026-07-12) flagged this as a shallow-seam problem: the same domain concept (period for a date) is computed independently at four call sites, and two of those derivations have already been caught disagreeing in production-adjacent testing (see rosterbot-2bl, rosterbot-ren).
design: Consolidate into one Period Resolver module in internal/fantrax with a single interface for resolving a date to its authoritative scoring period. cmd/optimize.go, internal/gscheck, matchup_weeks.go, and recent_stats.go all resolve through it instead of re-deriving. AnchorPeriodForDate-style anchoring on todays current period stays as the near-today strategy inside the resolver; PeriodForDate-style day math stays as the fallback inside the resolver -- the point is one place picks between them, not four.
acceptance_criteria: Single ResolvePeriod-style entry point exists in internal/fantrax. cmd/optimize.go GS-budget block and internal/gscheck.RunGSCheck both resolve period through it (no independent re-derivation). The scenario rosterbot-2bl describes (matchupWeekRanges position count silently desyncing from the real ScoringPeriod number on a back-to-back rematch) is provably impossible after the change, not just verified-absent-this-season. rosterbot-rens near-today Class A behavior is unaffected; the resolver is the structural host the season-wide historical date-to-period map (Class B) can be built into as a follow-on.
notes:
Implemented as fantrax.ResolvePeriod(periods, currentPeriod, seasonStart, today, date) in internal/fantrax/period_resolver.go -- three-tier fallback (authoritative periods list -> anchor arithmetic -> day math). cmd/optimize.go's lineup-apply path (former local resolveDatePeriod, now deleted) migrated to call it. Tests moved from cmd/optimize_period_test.go to internal/fantrax/period_resolver_test.go, closer to the logic.

Scoping decision (reviewed 2026-07-12, code-reviewer subagent): internal/gscheck.RunGSCheck and cmd/optimize.go's GS-budget block were deliberately NOT routed through ResolvePeriod. Both already source period from the same GetScoringPeriodsAndTeams() authoritative list via role-specific selectors (FindJustEndedPeriod, FindCurrentPeriod) for different questions than "what period is date X" -- they agree with ResolvePeriod's tier 1 by construction. Routing the safety-critical GS-budget gate through a function with weaker anchor/day-math fallback tiers would have been a behavior change to already-shipped, already-verified code, not a genuine dedup. Reviewer confirmed this reasoning holds.

Review also surfaced (and this PR's CLAUDE.md now documents accurately) a separate, real, NOT-yet-fixed bug in internal/fantrax/gs_check.go's GetTeamGS: its internal periodFor closure uses day-by-day anchor arithmetic that mis-derives the period number for every day within a merged multi-day scoring period except the one nearest the anchor (see TestFindCurrentPeriod_MergedAllStarBreakPeriod's period-16 fixture, 2026-07-13 to 2026-07-26 -- this season's real All-Star break, starting the day after this issue closed). Filed as a separate urgent follow-on rather than folded into this issue's scope.
close_reason: fantrax.ResolvePeriod implemented, tested, code-reviewed, and wired into cmd/optimize.go's apply path. See notes for the deliberate GS-budget/gscheck scoping decision and a newly-discovered follow-on bug filed separately.

title: Build exact date→period map for historical recap/backtest (period-drift Class B)
description:
Fantrax inserts extra daily scoring periods mid-season (doubleheader / postponed-game makeups), so PeriodForDate(seasonStart, date) -- which assumes one period per calendar day -- drifts behind Fantrax's authoritative numbering by the insertion count. Confirmed in 2026: matched through 06-07, off by one by 06-23.

Class A (near-today, action-affecting) is already fixed: fantrax.AnchorPeriodForDate(today, currentPeriod, date) anchors on Fantrax's authoritative current period, used by cmd/optimize.go's resolveDatePeriod and internal/fantrax/gs_check.go's GetTeamGS.

Class B (historical reporting) is still open: DailyFantasyPoints (internal/fantrax/daily_fpts.go, used by recap/recap-site/backtest/grade) and GetTeamPitcherStarts (internal/fantrax/pitcher_starts.go, used by recap/recap-site) still use season-start day math. A naive today-anchor fix would break early pre-insertion weeks in the weekly recap-site full rebuild (it re-derives every completed week each Monday) -- neither a season-start anchor nor a today anchor is globally correct across insertion boundaries. Needs an authoritative season-wide date-to-daily-period map.

Migrated from .scratch/period-drift/issues/01-historical-period-date-map.md (predates the bd migration, never ported over).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run 'go run . recap-site --out dist' (or 'go run . backtest --dates 2026-06-01:2026-06-30') covering a range that spans an insertion boundary, e.g. 2026-06-07 through 2026-06-23.
2. For each date, compare the period number DailyFantasyPoints derives via season-start day math against Fantrax's authoritative scoring-period number for that same date (visible via the Fantrax UI or getStandings' period captions).
3. Observe the two agree through 2026-06-07 and are off by one starting 2026-06-23, after Fantrax inserted an extra daily period for a doubleheader/postponed-game makeup.
4. Days/GS attribution in the affected week's recap or backtest report will be pulled from the wrong scoring period as a result.
acceptance_criteria:
recap-site full rebuild: every week's daily FP/GS attribution matches Fantrax-authoritative scoring across insertion boundaries (week-1 and a post-insertion week both correct in one build). backtest --dates <historical-range> grades the correct days. No per-day extra network calls on the hot path (map must be cached, season-stable).

Investigation notes: the roster API (getTeamRosterInfo) addresses purely by period number, no date param -- the period's date may live in the opaque TeamRosterResponse DisplayedSelections/MiscData blobs (parsed as map[string]interface{} in go-fantrax), needs spelunking, possibly a go-fantrax change to expose it. Alternative: probe period snapshots to discover insertion boundaries (offset is a non-decreasing step function), then encode the piecewise map.
notes: From memory period-drift-2026 and the pre-bd .scratch/ tracker. Class A fix reference: cmd/optimize.go resolveDatePeriod, internal/fantrax/gs_check.go GetTeamGS, fantrax.AnchorPeriodForDate.
close_reason: WeeklyPeriod/DailyPeriod type split landed; historical FP/GS walks now resolve dates via the authoritative periodList map (dailyPeriodForDate). Class-A unification deferred to rosterbot-2ax.

title: Team-abbreviation normalization inconsistently applied between projection and schedule paths
description: internal/projections normalizes the Fantrax team via NormalizeTeam before using it as a lookup key (projKey), but the schedule/probable-starter path compares the RAW p.MLBTeam field against normalized map keys (cmd/optimize.go:527,558; internal/optimizer/lineup.go:260). Verified live on 2026-07-10 that Fantrax currently returns canonical abbreviations for all 30 teams (including the recent OAK->ATH rename) matching NormalizeTeam's output, so this is NOT currently causing incorrect behavior. But it's a latent coupling: if Fantrax or MLB statsapi ever diverges on an abbreviation again (exactly the class of change OAK->ATH already was), the schedule-matching path would silently mark that team as 'no game' and bench every one of its hitters, with no error or warning surfaced anywhere.
acceptance_criteria: Normalize once at construction time in internal/fantrax/client.go, at the ~3 sites that set MLBTeam from MLBTeamShortName/TeamShortName, so every downstream consumer (projection AND schedule paths) sees the same canonical form. NormalizeTeam is already idempotent so this is safe to apply at the earliest point without touching the projection path's existing correctness.
notes: From fantasy-baseball-strategist review, 2026-07-10 (finding #4). Defensive hardening, not an active bug.
close_reason: Already fixed in commit b1a7635 (PR #38, merged 2026-07-12) — Normalize() moved to internal/teams and applied at all 5 upstream construction sites.
