comments.text:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Team abbreviations are normalized to a canonical form in one part of the lineup pipeline (projections) but compared in raw form in another part (schedule/probable-starter matching), which currently produces correct results only because the upstream data happens to already be in canonical form — a latent fragility rather than an active bug.

**Current behavior:**
Player records carry a team abbreviation sourced from the roster provider. One consumer normalizes this abbreviation before using it as a lookup key; another consumer (matching a player's team against today's game schedule) compares the raw, un-normalized abbreviation directly against schedule data. Today these happen to agree for all 30 teams, so nothing is currently broken. If the roster provider and the schedule data source ever diverge on an abbreviation for the same team again (this has happened before with at least one real-world team rebrand), the schedule-matching consumer would silently treat every player on that team as not playing that day, with no error or warning.

**Desired behavior:**
Team abbreviations should be normalized once, at the point they're first read from the roster provider, so every downstream consumer — including the schedule/probable-starter matching path — sees the same canonical form without needing to remember to normalize it themselves.

**Key interfaces:**
- The roster-provider client code that first populates a player's team-abbreviation field (there are a small number of call sites that do this from slightly different upstream field names).
- The existing team-normalization function is already idempotent, so applying it earlier is safe even where it's redundant with later normalization.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] All call sites that populate a player's team abbreviation from upstream data apply the existing normalization function before storing it.
- [ ] The projection-lookup path (which already normalizes) is unaffected — applying normalization twice is a no-op.
- [ ] New test coverage exists that would fail today's raw-comparison path (using a synthetic abbreviation mismatch) and passes once normalization happens at the source.

**Out of scope:**
- Changing the normalization mapping itself (which abbreviations map to which canonical form) — only where/when normalization is applied.

title: GS budget gate ceil-rounds fractional future SP demand, can over-suppress today's certain starts
description: internal/optimizer/gs_budget.go:164, applyGSGate: estCount := int(math.Ceil(futureEstimated)) turns a fractional rotation-math estimate for a future day without announced probables (e.g. 0.2 expected starts) into a full placeholder entry valued at the roster-wide mean SP projection, competing at FULL value against today's confirmed starters in the value-ranked gate. Combined with valuing every estimated future start at the roster-SP mean (not discounted for its lower certainty), this overstates future claims on the remaining weekly GS budget and can bench a certain, real start today in favor of a future start that may never materialize (probables not yet announced, rainout, roster move, etc). Only fires when GS_TRACKING_ENABLED and the weekly budget is genuinely tight, so scoped, but real when it does.
acceptance_criteria: Value estimated future starts at their fractional expectation rather than ceil-rounding to full placeholder entries (e.g. weight the placeholder's contribution to the ranking by the fractional amount rather than creating a full extra competing entry), and/or add a small certainty premium to today's confirmed starts so near-ties resolve toward the sure thing. The existing exact-tie 'prefer today' rule (gs_budget.go:185-189) already establishes the right intuition — extend it to near-ties, not just exact ones.
notes: From fantasy-baseball-strategist review, 2026-07-10 (finding #2). CLAUDE.md's GS-budget section has been corrected in this same session to describe the actual value-ranked gate (it previously described a since-superseded proportional-split formula).
close_reason: Fixed: estimated future GS demand now weighted by fractional share (not ceil-rounded to a full-value placeholder), and a 10% certainty margin extends the exact-tie today-preference rule to near-ties. Confirmed future starts unaffected. 3 new regression tests.

comments.text:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** The weekly game-start budget gate treats an uncertain, fractional future pitching-start estimate as a full-certainty competing claim on the remaining budget, which can cause it to suppress a today's confirmed start in favor of a future start that may never happen.

**Current behavior:**
When the gate needs to decide which scheduled starts to allow within a limited remaining weekly budget, it ranks all known and estimated starts by value and keeps the top N. For future days where the actual starters aren't announced yet, the code estimates a fractional expected number of starts (e.g., 0.2) based on roster composition, but then rounds that fractional estimate UP to a whole number of full-value placeholder entries before ranking. A day with only a 20% chance of producing a start is therefore treated as a certain, full-value start competing equally against today's already-confirmed starts.

**Desired behavior:**
An uncertain future start's claim on the budget should scale with its actual probability/fractional weight rather than being rounded up to a full competing entry. Today's confirmed, certain starts should have some degree of preference over equally-valued-but-uncertain future estimates, not just in exact ties.

**Key interfaces:**
- The budget-gate's future-demand forecasting, which already distinguishes "confirmed starters" from "estimated/fractional starters" per future day.
- The ranking step that decides which starts survive the budget cut.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] A future day's fractional/estimated start demand contributes to the ranking proportionally to its fractional value, not as one or more full-value placeholder entries.
- [ ] When a today start and a future estimated start are close in value (not just exactly equal), the gate prefers keeping today's start.
- [ ] Existing behavior for fully-confirmed starts (today and future) is unchanged.
- [ ] Existing test coverage for this gate is extended to cover a fractional-estimate scenario that would have previously over-suppressed a today start.

**Out of scope:**
- Changing how the roster-wide mean placeholder value itself is computed, or how confirmed future starters are weighted — only the fractional-vs-rounded-up treatment and near-tie preference are in scope.

title: Non-starter SP discount (0.10x) likely too generous for future-date/--matchup planning
description: internal/optimizer/pitcher_lineup.go:67 values a non-probable SP whose team plays at 10% of a full start. A projected-20-pt starter then shows as 2.0 pts, which can exceed a real RP's full projection and slot the SP (who most likely won't actually pitch that day) over an RP who will. Impact is muted for the daily production run (real probables are usually known, so real starters get full value), but it distorts --matchup/future-date planning where probables aren't yet announced. This is a repeat finding — flagged in a March 2026 audit and still unresolved.
acceptance_criteria: Lower the non-starter discount from 0.10x to something in the 0.03-0.05x range, or make it a function of how many days out the projection is (probables are announced ~1-5 days ahead for most teams; days further out should discount harder). Verify against backtest --matchup replays that the change doesn't regress lineups where the discount currently happens to work out.
notes: From fantasy-baseball-strategist review, 2026-07-10 (finding #3), confirmed unchanged since a March 2026 audit.
close_reason: Lowered non-starter SP discount from 0.10x to 0.05x (top of suggested 3-5% range), extracted as exported optimizer.NonStarterSPDiscount so backtest.go's mirrored discount can't drift independently (was a duplicated magic number). Regression test proves a 20pt/G non-starting SP no longer outranks a modest 1.1pt/G real RP. Note: did not build a full old-vs-new forward-planning replay harness (would require point-in-time projection snapshots this repo doesn't capture for what-if comparisons) - verified via unit regression test + full suite, not a live historical backtest replay.

> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** The point-value discount applied to a pitcher who isn't a confirmed starter (but whose team is playing) is likely too generous when used for forward-looking/multi-day planning, letting a probably-not-pitching starter outrank a reliever who will definitely play.

**Current behavior:**
A non-confirmed starting pitcher is valued at a fixed 10% of their full-start projection. For same-day decisions this rarely matters because actual starters are usually confirmed by the time the lineup runs. For multi-day-ahead planning, where confirmed starters aren't yet known for later days, this 10% figure can put a high-projection starter's discounted value above a lower-projection but definitely-playing reliever's full value, resulting in a lineup slot given to a pitcher unlikely to actually play.

**Desired behavior:**
The discount for an unconfirmed starter should be low enough that it doesn't generally outrank a real, confirmed relief option, while still being nonzero so a genuinely likely starter isn't penalized to uselessness.

**Key interfaces:**
- The single constant/multiplier applied to a non-confirmed starter's projected value.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] The discount multiplier is reduced from its current value into a smaller range (informally, somewhere around 3-5% rather than 10% is a reasonable starting point, but pick a specific value and justify it).
- [ ] Replaying recent multi-day/matchup-period planning scenarios through the existing backtest tooling shows no regression in realized lineup points versus the current behavior.
- [ ] Same-day behavior (where starters are already confirmed) is unaffected, since confirmed starters don't go through this discount path at all.

**Out of scope:**
- Making the discount vary by how many days out the projection is (a fixed constant is fine for this pass) — that's a reasonable future refinement but a separate, larger change.

title: ATC RoS FanGraphs projections (atc-ros) return zero rows for both bat+pit — confirmed upstream 500, but pipeline has no visibility into it
description:
internal/projections.LoadPitcherProjections("atc-ros",...) and LoadBattingProjections("atc-ros",...) both return NoData=true / Len()=0 (confirmed live via a direct uncached package call, 2026-07-10). This is NOT a rosterbot bug: I loaded https://www.fangraphs.com/projections?type=ratc&stats=pit... and stats=bat... in a real browser and FanGraphs' OWN frontend makes the identical request (GET /api/projections?type=ratc&stats=bat|pit...) and gets a 500 from their own server for both. Our fgProjectionType mapping ('ratc') is correct; FanGraphs' backend is currently broken for the ATC RoS type (both roles), for reasons outside our control. steamer-ros, depthcharts-ros, and thebatx-ros all load fine (verified same test: Len 4667-5854 bat / 723-5854 pit range).

The real, fixable gap: the shadow/grade/report pipeline (internal/report's rankSystems, cmd/shadow.go's per-system capture) has no visibility into a system coming back with LoadResult.NoData=true. LoadPitcherProjections/LoadBattingProjections silently return an empty stub 'so the optimizer can still run' (correct for the live optimize path, which only ever uses one configured system) but shadow explicitly loops all 4 shadowSystems including atc-ros with no fallback (LoadPitcherProjections only chains RoS->preseason->CSV for a BASE system name; an explicit '-ros' input skips straight to a single API attempt then CSV). Per the model-auditor's independent M2 finding: report.rankSystems has no common-support/minimum-N guard, so a system silently grading projected=0 for every player can be misread as 'ATC is inaccurate' rather than 'ATC had no data that day' — actively misleading on the projection-site dashboard, and this has likely been happening silently every day since the outage started (Shadow's ECS task exits 0 regardless, since NoData isn't an error).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Re-check the FanGraphs endpoint periodically — this piece may self-resolve. 2) Add NoData visibility: either skip writing a shadow snapshot for a system+role that came back NoData (rather than writing a zero/empty one), or tag SnapshotPlayer with a HasProjection flag so report.rankSystems can exclude no-data systems from ranking instead of silently grading them as projected=0. 3) Surface a warning (log line or Pushover) when shadow's capture hits NoData for any of the 4 systems, so a future upstream outage on any system doesn't go unnoticed.
notes: Overlaps with fantasy-baseball-model-auditor's M2 finding (system-comparison ranking conflates coverage with accuracy) from the 2026-07-10 review — this issue supplies the confirmed concrete instance (atc-ros, both roles, upstream 500) plus root cause.

comments.text:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** The multi-system projection capture/comparison pipeline has no visibility when one of its FanGraphs projection systems returns no data, so a system-level outage silently produces misleading zero-value projections instead of a visible gap.

**Current behavior:**
When a projection system's API fetch returns no usable rows for a role (hitters or pitchers) — e.g. an upstream outage on the provider's side — the loader returns an empty-but-valid result rather than an error, by design (so the live optimizer, which only ever loads one configured system, degrades gracefully rather than crashing). The multi-system capture/comparison pipeline reuses this same loader for every system it captures, with no additional handling: it has no way to distinguish "this system genuinely has zero projected points for this player" (a real per-player fact) from "this system returned no data at all today" (a data-availability fact about the system). Downstream, whatever computes per-system accuracy rankings has no minimum-coverage guard, so a system with zero real data for a period can still be graded and ranked as if every player's true projection were zero.

**Desired behavior:**
A system-level "no data available" condition (as opposed to a legitimate per-player zero projection) should be distinguishable end to end: from the initial fetch, through whatever gets persisted for later grading, through the accuracy-ranking computation. A system that had no data for a given day/role should not be graded/ranked on that day/role at all — it should be excluded from that comparison rather than silently scored as if it projected zero points for everyone. Ranking logic that picks a "best" system for a given window/role should only consider systems that actually had data for a reasonable portion of that window, and should make it visible (in whatever the human-facing report/dashboard is) when a system is missing data rather than just omitting it silently.

**Key interfaces:**
- Whatever loader function fetches a named projection system's data returns a result that already distinguishes "empty because no data available" from "empty because this player has no projection" (an availability signal exists at the loader level today — the gap is that nothing downstream reads or propagates it).
- Whatever per-player record gets persisted for later grading (the projection "snapshot") should carry enough information to tell, in hindsight, whether the source system had real data for that player on that day, vs. a zero-filled placeholder.
- Whatever computes per-system accuracy/ranking across systems should skip a system for a given window/role when its data coverage for that window/role is effectively empty, rather than including it with a misleadingly perfect or terrible score.
- Whatever writes the daily multi-system capture should emit a visible warning (log line at minimum) when a system comes back with no data for a role, so a provider-side outage doesn't go unnoticed for an extended period.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] A day/role where a captured system had no real projection data is excluded from that system's accuracy ranking for that window, not graded as zero-point projections.
- [ ] The capture step logs (or otherwise surfaces) a clear warning when a system returns no data for a role, distinct from normal operation.
- [ ] Systems with sufficient real data are unaffected — no change to their grading/ranking behavior.
- [ ] Historical snapshots written before this change (which don't carry the new availability signal) are handled gracefully — treat them as "assume had data" so existing historical rankings don't silently change/disappear.

**Out of scope:**
- Fixing the actual upstream outage (external, not ours to fix) — confirmed via the provider's own site returning a server error for the same request, so this is transient/external.
- Adding retry/backoff logic for the upstream fetch itself.
- Changing which projection system the live (non-comparison) optimizer path uses — that path already only loads one system and isn't affected by this gap.

title: Harden optimize.go's period-number resolution to match gscheck's derivation
description:
Final whole-branch review of rosterbot-r10 (live Fantrax GS limits) found that cmd/optimize.go resolves the scoring-period number via GetMatchupWeekNumberForDate (a positional count over matchupWeekRanges' same-opponent date groupings), while internal/gscheck.RunGSCheck uses period.Number (parsed directly from Fantrax's own 'Scoring Period N' caption text). These are structurally independent derivations with no code-level guarantee of agreement -- matchupWeekRanges groups purely by consecutive same-opponent entries with no gap check, so a genuine back-to-back rematch against the same opponent would desync the position count from the real ScoringPeriod number, silently (GetGSLimits would still return valid data for the wrong period, no error/warning).

Verified directly against the live 2026 league (all 23 scoring periods this season, via GetScoringPeriodsAndTeams + GetMatchupWeekNumberForDate cross-check): zero mismatches, including period 16 (the All-Star break this whole effort was built for). So this does NOT manifest as a live bug this season -- filing as a hardening fast-follow, not a regression.

Suggested fix: source the period number in cmd/optimize.go's GS-budget block the same structurally-guaranteed way gscheck.go does -- via GetAllMatchupEntries()'s ScoringPeriod field (or an equivalent lookup keyed off today's date) instead of GetMatchupWeekNumberForDate's positional count. Before landing, verify MatchupEntry.ScoringPeriod is uniform across all entries within a single merged week (e.g. period 16's Jul13-26 span) -- not yet confirmed.
acceptance_criteria: Source the period number in cmd/optimize.go's GS-budget block the same structurally-guaranteed way internal/gscheck.RunGSCheck does -- via GetAllMatchupEntries()'s ScoringPeriod field (or an equivalent lookup keyed off today's date) instead of GetMatchupWeekNumberForDate's positional count. Before landing, verify MatchupEntry.ScoringPeriod is uniform across all entries within a single merged week (e.g. period 16's Jul13-26 span) -- not yet confirmed. Superseded in practice if rosterbot-z3b's Period Resolver lands first: consuming that resolver from cmd/optimize.go satisfies this issue directly, since both call sites would then share one derivation.
notes:
Resolved by earlier work, confirmed during rosterbot-z3b's code review (2026-07-12): the GS-budget block in cmd/optimize.go already sources its period number from ft.GetScoringPeriodsAndTeams() + fantrax.FindCurrentPeriod() -- the same structurally-guaranteed mechanism gscheck.go uses -- predating rosterbot-z3b's own changes. GetMatchupWeekNumberForDate/matchupWeekRanges (the positional-count derivation this issue described) is confirmed used only by internal/recap for an unrelated "matchup week number" label, never for period resolution, anywhere in the live codebase. The specific desync scenario this issue was filed for is provably impossible today.

Note: this did NOT happen via the literal mechanism this issue's acceptance criteria anticipated (consuming rosterbot-z3b's new fantrax.ResolvePeriod from the GS-budget block) -- z3b's reviewer judged that routing the already-correct, safety-critical GS-budget gate through a function with weaker fallback tiers would be a behavior change, not a genuine dedup, so it was deliberately left as-is. Closing on the substance (the described bug scenario is moot) rather than the anticipated mechanism.
close_reason: GS-budget block already sources period via the authoritative periods-list lookup (predates rosterbot-z3b); GetMatchupWeekNumberForDate confirmed unused for period resolution anywhere live. See notes.

title: Surface GS-gate suppressed starts — make dead pitcher capital visible
description: applyGSGate already knows exactly which starters it flipped IsStarter=false, but that information is never surfaced. Logging suppressed-start count and total suppressed projected points per matchup week would turn the roster-shape question from an estimate into a measurement. This matters because the league config makes surplus SP structurally hard to deploy: verified from live cache, this league has 13 active hitter slots (C/1B/2B/3B/SS/INF/4xOF/3xUT) versus only 6 undifferentiated P slots, and a weekly game-start cap on top. Above the cap an extra ace start produces exactly zero marginal points. The gate firing regularly IS the signal that a roster owns more SP than the league permits it to deploy — currently that signal is computed and discarded.
acceptance_criteria: Weekly summary reports suppressed-start count and forgone projected points. Ideally also a roster-shape line: hitter vs pitcher value against slot counts and the cap.

title: Infra gap detection false-positives on days with no MLB games (All-Star break)
description:
The Infra tab reports 'missing days' for analysis/grades/ on dates where no fantasy-relevant MLB games were played, so there is nothing to grade and the absent partition is correct, not a fault.

Observed 2026-07-27: Infra reported 4 missing days for analysis/grades/ -- 2026-07-01, 2026-07-13, 2026-07-14, 2026-07-15 -- labelled 'Re-runnable'. Only 07-01 was a real gap (backfilled the same day, see notes). The other three are the All-Star break, confirmed against statsapi:

  2026-07-13  0 games
  2026-07-14  1 game   (the All-Star Game -- exhibition, no fantasy stats)
  2026-07-15  0 games
  2026-07-16  1 game   (graded, ~400-byte partitions)
  2026-07-17  15 games (normal slate resumes)

backtest --dates 2026-07-13:2026-07-15 returns 0.00 actual for all three days. grade correctly writes nothing, so the dt= partition never appears and gapsForPartitionedSeries counts a hole.

Cost of leaving it: the Infra page cries wolf once a season, and worse, 'Re-runnable' invites someone to re-run grade for those dates, which silently does nothing and looks like a second failure. The one genuinely broken day (07-01) was hidden in the same list as three false positives.
design:
Three options, none obviously right -- the tension is that internal/lineupapi deliberately has no MLB-schedule dependency and runs in a Lambda with s3:ListBucket only.

  A. Sentinel partition. Have grade write a zero-row grades.ndjson (or a small marker object) for a date it intentionally skipped because there were no actuals. The series then has no hole and Infra stays green with no new dependency in the judgement path. Athena reads a zero-row NDJSON as zero rows -- harmless. Cost: the Analysis Store gains an 'intentionally empty' concept it does not have today, and a zero-row partition is indistinguishable from a truncated write unless the marker is explicit.

  B. Teach the detector the schedule. Give lineupapi the set of no-game dates. Correct, but puts an MLB-statsapi call (or a cached schedule artifact) inside a status endpoint whose whole design point is that it reads live and depends on nothing that can itself go stale. Adds network + IAM to the Lambda.

  C. Do nothing in code; document the break in the runbook. Cheapest, but the page stays wrong once a season and the 'Re-runnable' label stays actively misleading.

Leaning A -- it keeps the judgement pure and puts the knowledge where the knowledge already is (grade knows it found no actuals). Worth deciding whether the marker should be an empty partition or a distinct key so 'no games' and 'graded zero rows' stay distinguishable.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A date with no MLB games does not appear as a missing/gap day on the Infra tab for analysis/grades/.
2. A date that SHOULD have been graded and was not is still reported -- the 2026-07-01 case must not be suppressed by whatever fix lands.
3. Whatever signal is chosen is distinguishable from a truncated or failed write, not merely absent-vs-empty.
4. If the sentinel route is taken, Athena queries over rosterbot_analysis.grades are unaffected (zero rows, no schema change).
5. Unit-tested in lineupapi without AWS and without network, consistent with the rest of the infra judgement tests.
notes: Related backfill done 2026-07-27: analysis/grades/dt=2026-07-01/system=depthcharts-ros/ was genuinely missing because the shadow capture skipped 07-01 (snapshots-systems jumps 06-30 -> 07-02) and the durable archive only starts 07-02, so the other three shadow systems for that date are unrecoverable. The flat hourly snapshot .backtest/snapshots/2026-07-01.json survived and self-identifies as depthcharts-ros, so it was copied into snapshots-systems/system=depthcharts-ros/ and graded (20 rows). That copy was synced to S3 so the backfill is reproducible.

title: Extract OptimizeDates and Emit phases; express phase ordering in the types
description:
rosterbot-6rv criterion 2, the last two unextracted phases, and the criterion the whole issue was really about.

OptimizeDates is the ~310-line parallel errgroup pass over the date list. Emit is the tail: write snapshots, publish the read-only lineup JSON, print, compute the combined-move delta, skip zero-gain swaps, ApplyLineup, send Pushover.

Emit is the part that matters most — it is the only phase that mutates remote state, and its internal ordering is load-bearing: the zero-gain delta check must run before ApplyLineup (a cosmetic swap involving a locked player makes Fantrax atomically reject the whole payload), and snapshots must be written before publish. Today nothing but physical line order enforces either.
design:
The issue's stated principle is the acceptance bar here: 'Ordering that matters should be expressed by one phase consuming the previous phase's output type, not by line position.'

So OptimizeDates returns []dateResult and Emit consumes it; within Emit, the delta check should produce a typed decision that ApplyLineup requires as input, so 'apply without checking' is not expressible rather than merely discouraged.

Do this one LAST. It is the largest remaining piece and it sits on the live-write path — every other extraction shrinks Run and clarifies what Emit actually depends on, which makes this safer to attempt. Doing it first would mean doing it against 800 lines of ambient context.
acceptance_criteria:
1. OptimizeDates and Emit are phase functions; Run is composition and little else.
2. Emit's internal ordering is expressed through types — the zero-gain delta decision is an input ApplyLineup requires, not a check that merely happens earlier in the function.
3. Both phases have tests with a fake client, including that a zero-gain move set is not applied.
4. Idempotency invariant holds: two identical runs still report 'No changes needed'.
5. Dry-run output stays byte-identical, and make run-all passes.
notes: Attempt after the other rosterbot-6rv follow-ups land.
close_reason: Closed

title: Extract LoadInputs phase: the six sequential Fantrax fetches
description:
rosterbot-6rv criterion 2, one of the four unextracted phases. Run performs six sequential Fantrax fetches inline (~45 lines): hitter roster, active slots, hitter scoring weights, pitcher roster, pitcher slots, pitcher scoring weights — plus the current-period lookup and MLB handedness.

Each is a fetch-then-warn-then-continue block with its own error text. Grouping them into one LoadInputs phase returning a struct makes the set explicit, lets the failure policy be stated once instead of six times, and gives the downstream phases a single typed input to consume — which is how the ordering between phases stops being enforced by line position.
design:
One phase function returning an inputs struct (rosters, slots, both scoring weight sets, current period, handedness) plus whatever partial-failure signal the current code carries.

Worth checking during the work whether these can run concurrently — they are six independent GETs executed sequentially today, and the per-date optimize pass below them already uses errgroup. If they can, that is a latency win on every hourly run; if they cannot (Fantrax rate limits, auth_client concurrency safety), record why in the phase doc comment so the next person does not re-ask. The apply path is explicitly not concurrent-safe, but these are reads.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The six fetches live in a LoadInputs phase returning a typed struct.
2. Downstream phases consume that struct rather than free variables.
3. The partial-failure policy is stated once, and tested with a fake client.
4. Concurrency is either implemented or explicitly ruled out in the doc comment with a reason.
5. Dry-run output stays byte-identical.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lift the GS-budget fetch cascade out of Run into the GSBudget phase
description:
rosterbot-6rv, completes the GSBudget phase. PR #84 extracted the two computational units (countTodayStarts, buildGSForecast) but left the surrounding fetch cascade inline in Run — roughly 45 lines of else-if chain covering GetMatchupWeekBounds, GetTeamGS, the periods lookup, GetGSLimits, and a Pushover alert on live-limit-fetch failure.

That chain encodes real policy: each failure mode disables the gate rather than falling back to a stale number, and the GetGSLimits failure specifically fires a Pushover because silently degrading pitcher usage is worse than a noisy alert. None of it is tested, and the branch ordering matters.
design:
Fold the cascade into a GSBudget phase function that returns (*optimizer.GSBudget, error) or (nil, reason) and takes the fetch surface as a narrow interface — the same shape the extracted units already use.

The Pushover side effect should be returned as a decision rather than performed inside the phase, so the phase stays testable and cmd/Run owns the notification. Each disable path deserves a test: no matchup week, GS walk failure, periods failure, unresolvable period, live-limit fetch failure (asserting the alert is requested), and no configured max (a clean no-op, not an error).

Note there is no static fallback for the GS max by design — a fetch failure means the gate genuinely cannot run. Preserve that; do not introduce a default.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The GS fetch cascade lives in a phase function behind a narrow interface, not inline in Run.
2. Every disable path has a test, including that a live GS-limit fetch failure requests a Pushover alert and does not fall back to a stale limit.
3. The Pushover send is owned by the caller, not performed inside the phase.
4. Dry-run output stays byte-identical.
close_reason: Closed

title: Give renderDateResult an io.Writer so cmd owns stdout
description:
rosterbot-6rv criterion 4, remaining half. PR #84 moved the 277-line render block out of Run into display.go as renderDateResult, but it still calls fmt.Printf directly.

The criterion is 'Rendering moves out of orchestration entirely — Run returns a value, a separate module renders it. cmd owns stdout.' Half of that is done (the code left the orchestration function); the other half is that nothing can render to anywhere but os.Stdout, so the board is untestable without capturing process output.

Also applies to the other direct-print sites still in Run: the per-date warnings loop and the planned-moves block.
design:
Thread an io.Writer through renderDateResult and the remaining print sites, defaulting to os.Stdout at the cmd layer.

Once a writer is injectable, the board becomes golden-testable — which is worth more than the tidiness. The render code is ~280 lines of positional box-drawing where a one-space shift is invisible to any unit test but obvious in a diff, and today the only thing catching that is the manual baseline-binary comparison.

Consider whether Run should return a render model rather than calling the renderer at all. That is the fuller version of the criterion, but it is a larger change and can be a follow-up — an io.Writer alone unblocks the golden tests.
acceptance_criteria:
1. renderDateResult and the remaining in-Run print sites write to an injected io.Writer.
2. cmd supplies os.Stdout; nothing in internal/lineuprun references os.Stdout for board output.
3. At least one golden test renders a fixed dateResult to a buffer and asserts the exact output, so column drift is caught in CI rather than by eye.
4. Dry-run output stays byte-identical.
close_reason: Closed

title: Decide whether to collapse the two near-twin daily period resolvers and the two weekly axes into one Period Map
description:
DECIDE-FIRST issue. Most of this area has already been fixed; what remains may not be worth touching. The point of this issue is to reach a decision, not to assume the refactor is correct.

internal/fantrax currently exposes five live ways to answer "which period does this date belong to":

  1. PeriodForDate(seasonStart, date)                      recent_stats.go:137   free fn, naive day math
  2. AnchorPeriodForDate(anchorDate, anchorPeriod, date)   recent_stats.go:127   free fn, anchored day math
  3. (c *Client) DailyPeriodFor(...)                       gs_period_walk.go:43  Class A: map -> anchor -> dayMath
  4. (c *Client) dailyPeriodForDate(seasonStart, date)     period_date_map.go:101 Class B: map -> dayMath
  5. FindCurrentPeriod / FindJustEndedPeriod / FindMostRecentPastPeriod  gs_check.go:395  weekly axis

plus a SECOND, independent weekly notion in matchup_weeks.go (MatchupWeekBounds / MatchupWeekNumberForDate), derived from GetAllMatchups opponent-pairing runs rather than from the standings-caption ScoringPeriod list.

(3) and (4) are near-twins differing in exactly one thing: whether the AnchorPeriodForDate tier is consulted between the authoritative map and the naive day-math fallback. Which one a caller should use is knowledge held by the caller and defended by inline comments -- lineuprun.go:599-611 carries an explicit comment steering future editors away from the deleted ResolvePeriod and toward DailyPeriodFor.

Incident history in this exact area: rosterbot-uv6 (false league-wide Under Min GS alert at the All-Star break boundary), rosterbot-z3b (11-day duplicate lineup-notification flood, every hourly run), rosterbot-48z (silent lineup-apply failure masked as success). All three were "wrong period axis or wrong resolver passed".

WHAT IS ALREADY DONE -- do not re-litigate:
  - rosterbot-1i3 made the two axes distinct Go named types (WeeklyPeriod / DailyPeriod), so crossing them is a compile error.
  - rosterbot-ren routed historical/backtest lookups through the authoritative periodList date map.
  - rosterbot-2ax unified the Class A anchored path onto that same map.

Those closed the bug class. What is left is a shape question: two near-twin resolvers and two weekly axes still exist, and choosing between them is still caller knowledge.

Surfaced by the 2026-07-22 architecture review (candidate 5 of 7, explicitly flagged as needing a decision before any work).
design:
The candidate shape is a single PeriodMap module whose interface is the two axes and nothing else:

    Daily(date)  DailyPeriod
    Weekly(date) WeeklyPeriod

with the fallback tiers (authoritative periodList map -> anchor -> naive day math) as IMPLEMENTATION, and one documented degradation policy, rather than a caller-visible choice between resolver 3 and resolver 4.

Questions to answer before writing any code:
  1. Is the Class A / Class B split (anchor tier present vs absent) load-bearing, or an artifact? The deferral note behind rosterbot-2ax argued neither a season-start anchor nor a today anchor is globally correct across insertion boundaries for both consumer classes simultaneously. If that is still true, ONE Daily(date) cannot serve both and this issue should be closed wontfix with the reasoning recorded as an ADR.
  2. Are the two weekly notions (standings-caption ScoringPeriod.Number vs matchup-week bounds from GetAllMatchups) genuinely the same concept? If they are not, they need distinct names in CONTEXT.md, not unification. This may be the more valuable half of the issue.
  3. Now that the authoritative map exists and is season-stable-cached, how often do the fallback tiers actually fire in production? If effectively never, collapsing them is cosmetic and the risk of touching this code is not justified. If they fire at insertion boundaries, the policy deserves to be one tested thing.
  4. Does any caller legitimately need to know WHICH tier answered? (Diagnostics for the next drift incident might.)

Recommended first step is measurement, not refactoring: instrument or reason about tier-hit frequency against the live periodList map, then decide. If the answer is "collapse", the resulting module gets a CONTEXT.md entry naming Period Map as domain language.
acceptance_criteria:
Either:
  (a) A decision to collapse, with: one PeriodMap module owning both axes, fallback tiers internal, a single documented degradation policy, tests covering each tier and the insertion-boundary case, all existing callers migrated, and a CONTEXT.md entry for the term; or
  (b) A decision NOT to collapse, recorded as an ADR in docs/adr/ explaining why the Class A / Class B split is load-bearing -- so the next architecture review does not re-suggest it.

In both cases:
  - The two weekly notions (ScoringPeriod.Number vs matchup-week bounds) are either unified or given distinct documented names in CONTEXT.md.
  - No regression in the incident scenarios: All-Star-break merged period (TestFindCurrentPeriod_MergedAllStarBreakPeriod), per-day GS deltas non-zero across a week, and one lineup-apply date resolving to its own daily period.
close_reason: Decided (a) COLLAPSE, measurement-driven. Q1: split NOT load-bearing — live periodList map covers whole season (187 entries, 1:1 with calendar days, zero insertions in 122 elapsed days) and naive day math agrees on all 187 dates, so the anchor tier (the only difference between the two resolvers) never once helped, while its input lagged a day on 2026-07-16 and caused rosterbot-48z. Deleted AnchorPeriodForDate + Client.dailyPeriodForDate; one DailyPeriodFor(seasonStart, date) = map -> day math, independent of 'today'. Q2: the two weekly notions agree EXACTLY (23/23 weeks, same bounds AND numbering, incl. 12-day opener and 14-day All-Star merge) — same concept two ways, documented as Weekly Period / Matchup Week in CONTEXT.md rather than unified in code. Q3: fallback tiers effectively never fire (map covers the season; only a fetch failure misses). Q4: no caller needed tier provenance; not added. Key reframing: the merging Fantrax does (All-Star break) is WEEKLY-axis only — the daily axis has never merged, contra the old doc comments. CONTEXT.md gains a Periods section (Daily Period / Weekly Period / Period Map / Matchup Week). Verified: 33 pkgs pass, vet clean, live optimize --dry-run idempotent, --matchup spans merged period 16 and resolves distinct daily periods. Commit b8ef12b.

title: Collapse the 20 duplicated cached-fetch branches in internal/fantrax into one generic helper
acceptance_criteria:
1. The if c.cacheDir == "" branch appears once, inside the shared helper, not 20 times.
2. Every previously-cached method still uses the same cache key and the same TTL as before -- verified by inspection of the key/tier arguments and by cache-hit behaviour under make run-all.

title: Split the 1201-line lineuprun.Run into named phases behind one interface
description:
internal/lineuprun.Run spans lineuprun.go:130-1330 -- 1201 lines performing at least 17 orthogonal responsibilities in a fixed sequence:

  1  set the global projection system            10  compute the GS budget (~140 lines, a sub-pipeline)
  2  construct the progress display              11  parallel per-date fetch + optimize (~310 lines, errgroup)
  3  resolve --dates all / --matchup ranges      12  write projection snapshots
  4  load hitter + pitcher projections, notify   13  publish the read-only lineup JSON
  5  roster IL/Minors alert + print to stdout    14  ANSI terminal rendering (~280 lines)
  6  six sequential Fantrax fetches              15  compute combined-move delta, skip zero-gain swaps
  7  fetch current + weekly scoring periods      16  ApplyLineup (remote state mutation)
  8  build blended projection sources            17  Pushover notification
  9  fetch MLB handedness

Specific interface problems:
  - Ordering between all 17 is enforced only by physical code order. Nothing at the type level prevents a future edit from publishing before snapshotting, or applying before the delta check.
  - cfg *config.Config is used as an OUTPUT parameter: Run appends resolved dates to the callers config at lineuprun.go:172 and :181. This is undocumented in the doc comment.
  - Options carries 12 fields, three of which (SnapshotFlag, ArchiveProjections, ForceSnapshot) encode one behaviour with back-compat aliases.
  - publish.go:35 reads os.Getenv("STATE_BUCKET") inline, so orchestration depends on the deployment environment.
  - Run both computes and renders: ~280 lines of box-drawing and ANSI colour sit inside the orchestration function.

Test coverage is 5 functions across 2 files, all pure helpers (display_test.go: colorDelta, combinedMovesDelta, isZeroGainDelta; snapshot_test.go: buildSnapshot). Run itself, windowedHitterRecent, publishLineup, sendOptimizeNotify and the entire GS-budget sub-pipeline are unexercised -- and Run is the code path that writes to the live Fantrax roster.

Surfaced by the 2026-07-22 architecture review (candidate 2 of 7). This is the largest of the four filed and should be attempted after its two dependencies land.
design:
Name each phase as a module with its own interface; Run becomes the composition and nothing else.

Candidate phase split (to be sharpened during grilling, not taken as final):
  ResolveDates    -- returns the date list as a VALUE; stops mutating cfg
  LoadInputs      -- rosters, slots, scoring weights, periods, handedness
  BlendSources    -- pure: recent-stats blending into projection sources
  GSBudget        -- pure given fetched inputs: matchup bounds, past GS, forecast, gate
  OptimizeDates   -- pure per date, parallelised by the composition
  Emit            -- snapshot, publish, apply, notify

Principles for the split:
  - A phase earns its place if it can be tested through its own interface without a fake Fantrax. GSBudget and BlendSources should come out fully pure; that is where the real leverage is.
  - Rendering moves out of orchestration entirely -- Run returns a value, a separate module renders it. cmd owns stdout.
  - Ordering that matters should be expressed by one phase consuming the previous phases output type, not by line position.
  - Options shrinks: the three snapshot flags collapse to one resolved decision made in cmd, and the deprecated aliases (--archive-projections, BACKTEST_ARCHIVE=1) are resolved at the flag layer rather than carried into the engine.
  - Both callers (cmd/optimize.go single pass, cmd/shadow.go four-system loop) must keep working; shadow is the reason Result exists and is the useful second caller that will keep the composition honest.

Dependencies: the Fantrax-interface issue supplies the seam phase tests need; the State Store issue removes the os.Getenv read from publish.go. Doing this first would mean doing both of those badly along the way.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Run no longer mutates the callers *config.Config; resolved dates are returned or passed as a value.
2. Each named phase is a module with its own interface and its own tests.
3. GS-budget logic and projection blending are testable without network or credentials.
4. Terminal rendering is no longer performed inside the orchestration function.
5. Options loses the redundant snapshot flags; the deprecated --archive-projections / BACKTEST_ARCHIVE=1 aliases still work from the cmd layer.
6. cmd/optimize.go and cmd/shadow.go both still work, including shadows four-system loop and its no-data transition detection.
7. Idempotency invariant holds: running optimize twice with the same inputs still reports "No changes needed" for all dates (per CLAUDE.md Idempotency section).
8. go vet ./... , make test and make run-all pass; a --dry-run optimize produces byte-identical output to the pre-refactor build for the same inputs.
notes:
UMBRELLA. Four of the five blocking issues landed on branch refactor/lineuprun-phases (2026-07-26): rosterbot-rr1, rosterbot-t89, rosterbot-32a, rosterbot-6om. Run is 716 lines, down from 838 after PR #84 and 1201 originally (-40%).

Criteria 2, 3 and 4 are now fully met:
  2 — phases with their own interfaces + tests: ResolveDates, LoadInputs, BlendSources, ComputeGSBudget (OptimizeDates/Emit remain, see rosterbot-k0n)
  3 — GS logic and blending both testable without network or credentials
  4 — rendering out of Run AND behind an injected io.Writer, with testdata goldens

Remaining: rosterbot-k0n (OptimizeDates + Emit, ordering expressed in types) — now unblocked, and it is the live-write path so it goes last.

Conventions the four landed phases established, worth holding k0n to:
  - side effects returned as decisions, not performed (GSAlert, Logs []string)
  - failure policy stated once per phase, tested branch by branch
  - concurrency allowed only where log emission and error precedence stay in fixed order

title: Deepen State Store selection: collapse 10 hand-rolled STATE_BUCKET branches into one module
description:
The decision "S3 when STATE_BUCKET is set, else a local directory" is re-implemented at 10 call sites across two packages, each returning a different concrete store type. The branch itself is copy-pasted; only the store type and prefix differ.

  cmd/root.go:95                cache.Store          (cache/ prefix)
  cmd/grade.go:131              analysis.Writer      (analysis/grades/)
  cmd/team-values.go:102        teamvalue.Writer     (analysis/team-values/)
  cmd/projection-site.go:44     analysis.Reader
  cmd/projection-site.go:105    teamvalue.Reader
  cmd/ledger.go:78              runWriter            (runs/)
  cmd/output.go:22              lineupapi.OutputWriter
  cmd/notifications.go:20       lineupapi.NotificationWriter
  cmd/progress.go:24            lineupapi.ProgressWriter
  internal/lineuprun/publish.go:35  lineupapi.Publisher

Two further variants: cmd/sync.go:53,77 gate whole sync loops on the same env var, and cmd/migrate_run_ledger.go:42 errors instead of falling back.

Consequences today:
  - The deployment story (which prefixes exist, what the local fallback root is, that Fargate sets STATE_BUCKET) is knowledge every call site must hold rather than a fact one module owns.
  - internal/lineuprun reads os.Getenv directly (publish.go:35), so an orchestration package depends on the deployment environment. This is one of the things that makes lineuprun.Run untestable -- see the Lineup Run phase-split issue.
  - Adding an eleventh durable artifact means writing the branch again and getting the prefix right by inspection.

Surfaced by the 2026-07-22 architecture review (candidate 1 of 7).
design:
One module owns the choice; every call site takes a Store it was handed.

  internal/statestore (or an equivalent home) exposes something like:
      For(prefix string) (Store, error)
  and owns: the STATE_BUCKET lookup, the S3-vs-file adapter choice, the prefix layout, and the local fallback root.

Two real adapters already exist and justify the seam (S3 on Fargate, filesystem locally), and tests gain a third (in-memory) for free.

Open design questions for the grilling pass:
  - The 10 sites want different typed stores (cache.Store, analysis.Writer, lineupapi.Publisher, ...). Does statestore return a byte-level store that each domain wraps, or a small set of typed constructors? The byte-level answer composes better with the pass-through-wrapper cleanup filed separately.
  - Where does it live so internal/lineuprun can depend on it without pulling the AWS SDK into a leaf? The existing cachestore/s3store and ndjsonstore/s3ndjson split is the precedent to follow.
  - Should the env read happen once at startup (initApp) and be passed down, rather than lazily at each For() call? Passing it down is what actually removes the environment dependency from lineuprun.

Compatible with ADR-0001: this changes where the choice is made, not what backs the Cache Store. S3-for-key-to-blob stands.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The os.Getenv("STATE_BUCKET") store-selection branch appears exactly once in the codebase (grep confirms; the sync.go gating and migrate_run_ledger.go variants either route through it or are explicitly documented as different).
2. internal/lineuprun no longer reads os.Getenv -- publish.go receives its publisher/store from the caller.
3. Prefix layout for every durable artifact (cache/, analysis/grades/, analysis/team-values/, runs/, lineup/, claims/, archive/, backtest/) is declared in one place.
4. Unit tests exercise at least one previously-untested call path with an in-memory store.
5. No behaviour change: a local run and a STATE_BUCKET run write to the same locations as before.
6. go vet ./... , make build-modules and make test pass; make run-all completes clean.
notes: Implemented + PR open: https://github.com/nixon-commits/rosterbot/pull/81 (branch rosterbot-9s6-statestore, 6 impl commits). Whole-branch review clean (Ready to merge=Yes). Close on merge. Follow-up filed: rosterbot-9th (BACKTEST_ARCHIVE).

title: Log a confirmation line when verifyExcludedRetry passes (silent success is indistinguishable from skipped)
description:
verifyExcludedRetry (internal/fantrax/apply_lineup.go) returns nil silently on BOTH the success path (re-fetched roster, all non-excluded changes confirmed landed) and the skip path (fetch == nil, or len(excluded) == 0). In production logs the two are indistinguishable — neither emits anything, and the caller just prints 'Lineup applied successfully.'

Only the two failure paths log: a re-fetch error logs 'post-retry verify skipped', and a genuine mismatch returns an error the caller surfaces as 'post-retry verify failed' + Pushover.

Found while auditing the live firing on 2026-07-20 20:01:38 PDT (period 118): the retry excluded 5 locked players (Arozarena, E.Rodriguez, J.Rodriguez, Hoerner, Crews), then logged 'Lineup applied successfully.' Confirming that the verify actually RAN — rather than silently no-op'ing — required grepping that internal/fantrax/client.go:722 is the sole production caller and always wires a non-nil fetch closure. That is inference from source, not evidence from logs.

Risk: if a future caller of applyLineupWithLockedPlayerRetry passes nil fetch, the 48z protection silently degrades to a no-op and production logs look identical to the working case. That is the same false-confidence failure mode rosterbot-48z was filed about — a success path that lied for 3+ consecutive hourly runs.
design: Three options considered: (1) always log on success — auditable every run, costs one line per retry in the hourly cron; (2) gate on Verbose — keeps output clean but production still cannot distinguish the two silent paths, defeating the purpose; (3) leave it and instead add a test asserting the sole call site passes non-nil fetch — cheaper regression guard but still no positive production evidence. Leaning (1), optionally plus the test from (3). Retries are rare (one firing in the 6 days since the fix shipped 2026-07-16), so the log volume cost is negligible.
acceptance_criteria: A successful post-retry verify emits a positive log line naming how many changes were confirmed (e.g. 'fantrax: post-retry verify — N change(s) confirmed landed'), so 'verify ran and passed' is distinguishable from 'verify skipped' in CloudWatch. Decide explicitly whether to gate on Verbose (leaning NO — gating reintroduces the ambiguity in production, which is the whole point of the change). Optionally add a call-site test asserting fetch is non-nil so a future nil-fetch caller fails in CI rather than silently disabling the check.
notes: Follow-up to rosterbot-48z (PR #62, merged 2026-07-16). Verified during that audit: the fix itself is correct and working — fetch calls c.auth.GetTeamRosterInfoRaw directly, bypassing the 15m todayTTL roster cache, so the verify reads live state. All 4 verify paths have passing tests in internal/fantrax/apply_lineup_test.go. This issue is purely about observability of the success path, not a defect in the verify logic.
close_reason: Success path now logs 'post-retry verify — N change(s) confirmed landed (M excluded as locked)', unconditionally (NOT gated on Verbose — gating would reintroduce the production ambiguity the issue was about). Also split the collapsed 'fetch == nil || len(excluded) == 0' guard: no-retry stays silent by design (runs hourly, nothing to verify), but a nil fetcher WITH exclusions now logs 'post-retry verify DISABLED ... outcome unconfirmed', so a future caller silently disabling the 48z protection is visible in CloudWatch. Chose that over the optional call-site test: c.auth is a concrete *auth_client.Client, not an interface, so a real call-site test would need network — the runtime warning is stronger anyway since it's positive production evidence rather than a CI-only check. Commit c7e16e3 on fix/rosterbot-7lo-verify-success-log.

title: Extract lineup-run orchestration out of cmd/optimize.go into a testable internal package
description: cmd/optimize.go is 1483 lines mixing CLI flag wiring with core orchestration: period resolution (resolveDatePeriod), the GS-budget gate, the projection pipeline, snapshot writing, and print/apply. cmd/shadow.go needs to redirect runOptimizes snapshot output to a per-system path; the only seam available is captureSystemRoot, a package-level mutable var declared in optimize.go and set/cleared from shadow.go. title: Manual-trigger API (POST /v1/jobs/{name}) has no in-flight check, can race scheduled EventBridge runs
description: POST /v1/jobs/{name} (infra/infra.go, ecs:RunTask launch handler ~line 218-234) launches a task on demand with no check for an already-running instance of the same job. Mostly benign since cache writes are last-write-wins, EXCEPT the claims cursor (internal/claims/run.go, persisted at .waivers/last-claims.json via CLAIMS_CURSOR_PATH) -- an overlapping manual + scheduled run there can both read the same cursor before either writes, producing duplicate Pushover notifications for the same claim events. Cosmetic (no data loss, no incorrect ledger state), but a real latent race. Per the Database Optimizer subagent's 2026-07-03 AWS storage audit (finding #3 of 3).
acceptance_criteria: Before ecs:RunTask in the manual-trigger handler, check GET /v1/runs (or the equivalent run-ledger query) for an in-flight run of the same job name and reject/no-op the manual trigger (with a clear API response) if one is already running. Verify by manually triggering the claims job while a scheduled run is in flight and confirming only one Pushover notification fires.
notes: Memory: aws-storage-audit-findings.
close_reason: Added an in-flight check to POST /v1/jobs/{name} (internal/lineupapi/handler.go handleJob + jobs.go inFlightRun): before launching, scans recent runs for a RUNNING entry whose command's first token matches the requested job name, and rejects with 409 if found. Matches on base job name (ignoring flags) per the acceptance criteria's 'same job name' wording, since the race (e.g. claims cursor) isn't specific to one param combination. Bounded by a 2h staleness window since entrypoint.sh only flips RUNNING->SUCCESS/FAILED after the command exits -- a hard crash mid-run would otherwise leave a ledger entry RUNNING forever and permanently block future manual triggers for that job, which would have been a worse regression than the race it fixes. Fails open (nil RunStore or a List error skips the check) since this is a race-reduction guard, not a strict lock, and local  runs without Runs configured at all. 8 new tests covering the pure inFlightRun logic (name matching, staleness, fail-open paths) plus full handler-level 409/202 wiring.

title: Legacy Analysis Store partitions (pre-system dimension) invisible to Athena ad-hoc queries
description:

title: No-projection blend fallback trusts raw 2-GP YTD at 100% weight
description:
internal/projections/blended.go:59-65 and pitcher_blended.go:66-72: when a player has no FanGraphs projection but has recent Fantrax stats, the blend returns recent.FPtsPerGame UNSHRUNK at 100% weight, gated only by GamesPlayed >= minGP (BLEND_MIN_GP, default 2). The shrinkage formula (seasonWeight = approxPA/(approxPA+250)) only applies on the path where a base projection also exists. So a just-called-up player who homers twice in 2 games gets projected as a season-long standout; scoreRoster (internal/optimizer/lineup.go:265-268) feeds that straight into the optimizer and the snapshot. Cold 2-game players are correctly benched near-zero, but hot 2-game players can be started over proven options — asymmetric risk concentrated exactly in the fringe/call-up population that waiver and streaming decisions hinge on.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Pick a player with no FanGraphs depthcharts-ros projection (a recent call-up) who went 2-for-4 with 2 HR in their first 2 MLB games.
2. Run the optimizer for a date after those 2 games with --projections depthcharts-ros (or call BlendedSource.GetPtsPerGame / PitcherBlendedSource.GetPitcherPtsPerGame directly in a unit test).
3. Observe the returned FP/G equals the raw 2-game recent.FPtsPerGame at full weight, with no shrinkage toward a league/positional baseline.
4. Compare to a player with an established 90+ GP sample and no base projection: their recent.FPtsPerGame is also returned unshrunk today, but the fix should leave that case materially unaffected while pulling the 2-game case toward a baseline.
acceptance_criteria: Regress the standalone recent value toward a positional/league-average baseline using the same n/(n+k) shrinkage idea (prior = league-avg FP/G at that position) instead of trusting it at 100%, or raise the projection-less minGP threshold to ~10-15 GP before treating raw YTD as a full projection.
notes: From fantasy-baseball-model-auditor review, 2026-07-10 (finding M1).
close_reason: Shrinkage now applied in the shared blend-core's no-base-projection fallback, regressing toward a league-average FP/G baseline (FanGraphsSource.AverageFPG / FanGraphsPitcherSource.AverageFPG) using the same n/(n+k) curve as the has-base-projection path. Implemented via the rosterbot-4lc extraction per its own notes. Also added shadow no-data transition alerting (closing the outstanding AC#3 from rosterbot-784).

comments.text:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** When a player has no season-long base projection available (e.g. a recent call-up) but does have a couple of games of recorded performance, that raw small-sample performance is used as their full point projection at 100% confidence, with no regression toward a more reasonable baseline — creating small-sample mirages that can distort start/sit and waiver decisions specifically for the fringe/recently-added player population where this matters most.

**Current behavior:**
The blending logic has two paths: when a player has both a base projection and recent performance data, recent performance is blended in with a weight that grows gradually with sample size (more games played → more trust in recent performance, per an established shrinkage formula). But when a player has no base projection at all, the fallback path skips this shrinkage entirely and uses the raw recent-performance rate directly, gated only by a low minimum-games threshold. A player with an outlier 1-2 game stretch (e.g., two home runs in two games) gets projected as if that rate would continue, rather than being pulled toward a realistic baseline.

**Desired behavior:**
The no-base-projection fallback path should apply comparable regression/shrinkage logic to what the has-base-projection path already does, so a tiny sample doesn't get trusted as a stable rate. A reasonable prior to regress toward is a league- or position-average rate, or simply the same shrinkage math promoted to a higher minimum sample size before trusting the raw rate at anything close to full weight.

**Key interfaces:**
- The no-base-projection fallback branch in both the hitter and pitcher blending logic (this pattern exists in both places and should be fixed consistently in both).

**Acceptance criteria:**

title: Move run ledger to its own S3 prefix (runledger/) instead of sharing runs/
description:
Follow-up to the /v1/runs pagination fix (PR #27, internal/lineupapi/s3lineup/runs.go). Root cause of that bug: the run ledger (runs/<invts>-<id>.json, listed by RunsStore.recent()) shares the runs/ S3 prefix with per-run output blobs (runs/<hex-id>/output.json, written by OutputStore). Lexicographic key ordering interleaves the two, so listing the ledger requires paginating past an ever-growing pool of unrelated output keys.

PR #27 fixed this on the reader side (recent() now follows NextContinuationToken instead of assuming a single page). That's correct and already deployed, but every /v1/runs and /v1/runs/{id} call still pages through however many output sub-keys happen to sort before the ledger records it needs - cost grows with total run count, not with `limit`.

This ticket is to actually separate the two into distinct prefixes so ledger listing goes back to being a cheap, bounded operation with no dependency on how many output blobs exist.
design:
- Add a new prefix (e.g. runledger/) for ledger records only; leave OutputStore on runs/<id>/output.json (output blobs are looked up by exact key via Get(), never listed, so they don't need to move).
- Update both call sites that construct RunsStore with s3lineup.NewRuns(ctx, bucket, "runs/"):
  - cmd/ledger.go:79 (the run-ledger CLI writer, PutRun)
  - lambda/main.go:42 (the read path, List/Get)
  Change both to "runledger/".
- One-time migration: copy existing runs/<invts>-<id>.json objects (NOT the runs/<hex-id>/output.json sub-objects) to runledger/<invts>-<id>.json in STATE_BUCKET. Can be a small one-off Go script or `aws s3api list-objects-v2` + filtered `aws s3 cp` loop (must exclude keys containing "/" after the runs/ prefix, matching the existing flat-key filter logic in RunsStore.recent()).
- After migration is verified (both old runs/*.json ledger keys and new runledger/*.json exist and /v1/runs still reports correctly against the new prefix), old runs/*.json ledger records can be left in place (harmless, no longer listed) or cleaned up later - not urgent since they're small flat JSON objects.
- Once runledger/ is confirmed to contain only flat ledger keys, recent() no longer strictly needs the "/" sub-key filter or even the pagination loop for correctness (only for scaling past 1000 total ledger records) - but there's no harm in leaving both, they're now just defensive rather than load-bearing.
- Verify old and new list against each other during cutover (e.g. run both prefixes' List side by side for a day) before removing the "runs/" writer path.
acceptance_criteria:
- Ledger writer (cmd/ledger.go) and reader (lambda/main.go) both point at runledger/ prefix
- Existing ledger records migrated from runs/*.json to runledger/*.json with no data loss (spot-check record count and a handful of IDs match)
- GET /v1/runs and /v1/runs/{id} verified live against the new prefix, newest-first, matching pre-migration output
- go test ./... passes with updated s3lineup tests reflecting the new prefix
close_reason: Shipped in #28 (merged aec08ed). Writer (cmd/ledger.go) and reader (lambda/main.go) both on runledger/; infra IAM updated; 409 ledger records migrated from runs/ to runledger/ (verified: independent count match 409=409, byte-identical spot check); GET /v1/runs and /v1/runs/{id} verified live post-deploy, newest-first. Follow-up rosterbot-q3b filed for optional cleanup of the now-orphaned old runs/*.json ledger keys.

title: Delete the pass-through NDJSON store wrappers and share one S3 blob adapter
description:
Lowest-payoff candidate of the seven from the 2026-07-22 architecture review -- filed for tracking, not as a recommendation to act soon.

Two separate observations, both about plumbing left over after the internal/ndjsonstore extraction.

(a) Shallow wrappers. internal/analysis and internal/teamvalue each expose a Writer interface + writer struct + two constructors, and a Reader interface + reader struct + two constructors -- eight constructors total across the two packages -- whose bodies forward exactly one call:

    analysis/grades.go:82   func (w writer) WriteGrades(date, system, rows) error {
                              return ndjsonstore.Write(w.store, objectKey(date, system), rows)
                            }
    analysis/reader.go:12   reader -> ndjsonstore.ReadAll with a decorate hook
    teamvalue/teamvalue.go, teamvalue/reader.go -- same shape, minus the system dimension

Deletion test: remove analysis.Writer and have callers hold an ndjsonstore.Store and call ndjsonstore.Write(store, analysis.ObjectKey(date, system), rows) directly -- no complexity reappears. The row type (GradeRow / Row), the partition-key logic (ObjectKey, SystemFromKey, LegacySystem) and the decorate hook DO earn their keep and must stay; only the wrapper indirection is shallow.

ndjsonstore itself is deep and should not be touched: Marshal/Unmarshal/Write/ReadAll with the mixed-depth partition walk that matches on filename suffix so one pass covers both dt=*/system=*/ and legacy dt=*/ layouts.

(b) Two S3 adapters duplicating AWS SDK plumbing:

    internal/cachestore/s3store/s3store.go     81 lines
    internal/ndjsonstore/s3ndjson/s3ndjson.go  92 lines

Both wrap config.LoadDefaultConfig in a New(ctx, bucket, prefix), both define a private api interface subsetting the S3 client, both build near-identical PutObjectInput / GetObjectInput with a prefix-joined key. They differ only in error mapping (NoSuchKey -> found=false vs a plain error), key suffixing (.json vs raw), and which extra operation they need (DeleteObject vs ListObjectsV2).

EXPLICITLY NOT DUPLICATION -- do not "fix" this: the two Store INTERFACES are genuinely different shapes and should stay different.

    cache.Store       Get(key) ([]byte, bool, error) · Put · Remove      -- keyed TTL cache: delete-capable, no enumeration
    ndjsonstore.Store Get(key) ([]byte, error) · Put · List(prefix)      -- append-only partitioned log: enumerable, no delete

Those signatures reflect real semantic differences between the Cache and the durable stores. Only the SDK plumbing beneath them is shared.

Surfaced by the 2026-07-22 architecture review (candidate 7 of 7, rated Speculative).
design:
Two independently shippable halves; either can be done without the other, and either can be declined.

(a) Drop the wrapper constructors. Keep GradeRow / Row, ObjectKey, SystemFromKey, LegacySystem, MarshalNDJSON and the decorate hook in their domain packages. Callers (cmd/grade.go, cmd/team-values.go, cmd/projection-site.go) hold an ndjsonstore.Store and call the package-level functions. Note this interacts with the State Store issue (rosterbot-9s6): if statestore returns a byte-level store, these call sites become a one-liner and the wrappers have even less to justify them. Sequence after 9s6 rather than before.

(b) Share one s3blob adapter under the two Store shapes: a common Put/Get/List/Delete over the AWS SDK, plus a thin shim per Store interface handling the not-found mapping and key suffixing. Roughly 100 of 173 lines collapse.

Caveat on (a): the wrappers are what currently make analysis and teamvalue reach ~94% and 100% coverage with in-memory stores. Removing them must not push that coverage onto untested cmd/ code -- if the wrappers are the reason the domain packages are well tested, keeping them is a defensible answer and this half should be declined.
acceptance_criteria:
Either half may be closed as declined with reasoning; not all of this needs doing.

If (a) is done:
  1. The eight pass-through constructors across analysis and teamvalue are gone; row types, ObjectKey, SystemFromKey, LegacySystem and the decorate hook remain in their domain packages.
  2. Coverage for internal/analysis and internal/teamvalue does not regress, and the logic does not migrate into untested cmd/ code.
  3. Legacy partition reads (dt=X/grades.ndjson with no system= segment, attributed to analysis.LegacySystem) still work -- verified against the projection dashboard.

If (b) is done:
  4. One S3 blob adapter backs both Store shapes; per-Store shims handle not-found mapping and key suffixing only.
  5. The AWS SDK stays out of internal/cache and internal/ndjsonstore leaves.
  6. ADR-0002 is amended to reflect a shared adapter, rather than being silently contradicted (it currently asks for an isolated S3 adapter per store).

Always:
  7. The two Store interfaces remain distinct shapes -- this issue must not unify cache.Store and ndjsonstore.Store.
  8. go vet ./... , make build-modules and make test pass; a real S3 read/write path is exercised at least once before merge.
close_reason: Half (b) shipped in PR #90 (fe3fa2c), merged to main: one shared internal/s3blob Blob under all ten S3-backed stores, per-store shims own only key layout + not-found policy, AWS SDK stays out of the internal/cache and internal/ndjsonstore leaves, the two Store shapes remain distinct (criterion 7 held), and ADR-0002 amended at docs/adr/0002:75-89 to say 'isolated Store shape, not an isolated copy of the SDK plumbing' (criterion 6). Half (a) DECLINED per this issue's own acceptance criteria ('either half may be closed as declined'): the eight pass-through constructors in internal/analysis and internal/teamvalue remain (analysis/grades.go:86, teamvalue/teamvalue.go:101). They are the documented seam cmd/ wires stores through and were the lowest-payoff item of the seven from the 2026-07-22 review; deleting them would push construction into untested cmd/ code, against criterion 2. Refile if that changes.

comments.text:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Rare in-game bonus events (a batter hitting for the cycle, a pitcher throwing a no-hitter or perfect game) aren't detected when reconstructing a player's historical single-day fantasy point total from raw box-score-style game logs, undercounting that day's points by the bonus amount whenever one of these rare events occurs.

**Current behavior:**
The league's scoring rules include bonus point values for these three rare single-game achievements. The regular projection and live-scoring paths correctly don't attempt to project them (they're unprojectable rare events). But the historical single-game reconstruction path — used to backfill a day's fantasy points from raw stats when needed (e.g. for a player's first day after a waiver pickup) — also doesn't check for them, even though it has access to the full single-game stat line needed to detect all three.

**Desired behavior:**
The historical single-game reconstruction path should detect all three events from the game's stat line and add the corresponding bonus points, so historical point totals are exactly correct even on the rare day one of these occurs.

**Key interfaces:**
- The single-game stat-line-to-points scorer used by the historical backfill path.
- Cycle detection needs at least one single, double, triple, and home run in the same game.
- No-hitter/perfect-game detection needs innings-pitched, hits-allowed, walks-allowed, and hit-by-pitch-allowed (perfect game additionally requires zero baserunners by any means) over a minimum of 9 innings.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Before implementing, confirm the league's actual configured point values for these three categories (they may already be zero, in which case this is a no-op and the issue should just be closed with that finding).
- [ ] If non-zero, a synthetic game line representing each of the three events is correctly detected and scores the bonus.
- [ ] A normal game log with none of these events is unaffected.

**Out of scope:**
- Adding these to the season-long or per-game projection paths (they remain intentionally unprojectable) — only the historical single-game backfill/reconstruction path is in scope.
